definition_zh: 分析；解析；化验；（数学）分析学；（精神）分析治疗
definition_en: the process of breaking a whole into its parts in order to understand it, or a detailed examination of something
core_image: 把一整块东西拆成零件，逐个看清它们如何咬合
scene: 实验室的灯亮到深夜，桌上摊着一份浑浊的水样报告。The chemist's analysis showed traces of mercury in the river water.
sceneCN: 这里 analysis 是「化验、解析」（第 1 个义项：把整体拆成部分来研究）；句意为化学家的分析显示河水里含有微量汞。画面里有试管、水样瓶与记录本。

pos.zh: 名词：分析；解析；化验；分析学

由词干加 -ist 构成，义为「分析师；化验员」
由词干加 -ic 构成，义为「分析的；解析的」
analytic 加 -al 构成，义为「善于分析的；分析性的」
analytical 加 -ly 构成，义为「以分析的方式」
analyze 加 -able 构成，义为「可分析的」

senses.title: Breaking a whole into parts
senses.titleCN: 拆解研究：把整体分成部分来理解
senses.definition: the process of examining something complex by separating it into its parts and studying how they relate
senses.definitionCN: 把复杂事物分成各个部分、研究其相互关系以理解整体的过程
senses.example: Her analysis of the poem focused on its images and rhythm.
senses.exampleCN: 她对这首诗的分析集中在意象与节奏上。
senses.why: Greek analyein meant to loosen up; an analysis loosens a whole until its parts can be seen separately.
senses.whyCN: 希腊语 analyein 意为「松开」，分析就是把整体松开，直到各个部分能单独看见。

senses.title: A laboratory test
senses.titleCN: 化验：对样品做成分检测
senses.definition: a chemical or medical test in which a sample is examined to find out what it contains
senses.definitionCN: 对样品进行化学或医学检测，以查明其中含有哪些成分
senses.example: A blood analysis revealed that she was short of iron.
senses.exampleCN: 一次血液化验显示她缺铁。
senses.why: The same loosening is applied to a sample: it is broken into measurable components until its makeup is readable.
senses.whyCN: 同样的「拆开」被用在样品上：样品被分成可测量的成分，直到成分变得可读。

senses.title: Psychoanalysis
senses.titleCN: 精神分析：梳理被压抑的心理材料
senses.definition: a method of treating mental distress by bringing buried feelings and memories into conscious view
senses.definitionCN: 通过把被埋藏的情绪与记忆带到意识层面来治疗心理困扰的方法
senses.example: He underwent analysis for two years after the loss.
senses.exampleCN: 失去亲人后，他接受了两年精神分析。
senses.why: Freud borrowed the word for the mind: what is buried is loosened and brought up into the light.
senses.whyCN: 弗洛伊德把这个词借来处理心灵：被埋藏的东西被松开，并被带到明处。

senses.title: Mathematical analysis
senses.titleCN: 数学分析：研究极限、级数与连续变化
senses.definition: the branch of mathematics that studies limits, continuity, series and related ideas
senses.definitionCN: 研究极限、连续性、级数及相关概念的数学分支
senses.example: The course begins with real analysis and then moves to complex functions.
senses.exampleCN: 这门课从实分析开始，然后讲到复变函数。
senses.why: In mathematics the parts being separated are limits and series, and the discipline that studies them is named for the separating.
senses.whyCN: 在数学里，被拆分的对象是极限与级数，研究它们的学科就以「拆分」命名。

senses.title: A written or spoken examination
senses.titleCN: 评析文章：成篇的分析
senses.definition: a written or spoken account that examines a subject in detail and explains how its parts work
senses.definitionCN: 对某一主题作细致考察、说明其各部分如何运作的书面或口头论述
senses.example: The magazine published a careful analysis of the election results.
senses.exampleCN: 这本杂志刊登了一篇对选举结果的细致分析。
senses.why: A written analysis repeats the same movement in prose: the subject is taken apart for the reader, piece by piece.
senses.whyCN: 书面分析用文字重复同一个动作：把研究对象为读者一块一块拆开。

intro.en: Analysis is a Greek word that reached English through Latin, and its image has always been the loosening of a whole into parts.
intro.cn: analysis 是经拉丁语进入英语的希腊词，它的意象始终是把整体松开、分成部分。

items.en: The verb lyein meant 'to loosen, release'. From it came lysis, 'a loosening', which forms the second half of the word.
items.cn: 动词 lyein 意为「松开、释放」，由它生出 lysis「松开」，构成这个词的后半部分。

items.en: Ana- added 'up, throughout, apart', so analyein meant 'to loosen up, dissolve', and analysis was 'a dissolving into parts'. Early uses were mathematical.
items.cn: ana- 加上「向上、贯穿、分开」的意思，于是 analyein 表示「松开、溶解」，analysis 就是「分解成部分」；早期多用于数学。

items.en: Latin borrowed analysis as a learned word from Greek and kept the sense of resolving a whole into its elements.
items.cn: 拉丁语把 analysis 作为学术借词从希腊语引入，保留了「把整体分解为要素」的意思。

items.en: In medieval and Renaissance Latin the word widened from mathematics to logic, medicine and chemistry.
items.cn: 在中世纪与文艺复兴时期的拉丁语里，这个词从数学扩展到逻辑、医学与化学。

items.en: English borrowed the word in the sixteenth century. The exact first written use is uncertain, and early spellings varied.
items.cn: 英语在十六世纪借入这个词；确切的首次书面使用不确定，早期拼写也有多种。

items.en: Chemistry, psychology and literary criticism each gave the word its own object, but the image of taking apart remained.
items.cn: 化学、心理学与文学批评各自给了这个词不同的对象，但「拆开」的意象一直保留。

note.en: The look-alike group holds words built on the same Greek stem; the near-meaning group holds acts of examining or judging that differ in scope.
note.cn: 形近组收同一希腊词干构成的一族词；近义组收考察与评判类词，彼此范围不同。

entries.definition: The verb meaning to separate something into parts and study them.
entries.definitionCN: 动词，义为「分析、解析」，即把事物分成部分加以研究。

entries.definition: A person whose job is to examine data, systems, or chemical samples.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，指以分析数据、系统或化验样品为业的人。

entries.definition: An adjective describing a method or mind that works by separating things into parts.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，形容以拆分部分来运作的方法或头脑。

entries.definition: The more common adjective form, meaning skilled at or based on analysis.
entries.definitionCN: 更常见的形容词形式，义为「善于分析的、分析性的」。

entries.definition: A close look at something, often less technical than an analysis.
entries.definitionCN: 对某物的仔细查看，通常不如 analysis 那样专业、系统。

entries.definition: A judgment of value or quality after weighing the evidence.
entries.definitionCN: 权衡证据后对价值或质量作出的评判。

entries.definition: An explanation of what something means, rather than how it is built.
entries.definitionCN: 对某物含义的解释，重点在意义而非构造。

entries.definition: The physical cutting apart of a body or idea into its parts.
entries.definitionCN: 把身体或观念实际切分开来、分成各部分。

normalIntro.en: These hooks fix the word through its sound, its spelling and the picture of taking something apart.
normalIntro.cn: 下面几个钩子从读音、拼写和「拆开」的画面三个方面固定这个词。

normal.en: Say it as 'a-NA-ly-sis': the stress falls on the second syllable, like a hammer landing on the part you want to split.
normal.cn: 读作「呃-NA-勒-西斯」，重音落在第二音节，像锤子敲在你想要劈开的那一处。

normal.en: The ending -sis marks a process, so analysis is the process of analysing, not the person doing it.
normal.cn: 结尾 -sis 表示过程，所以 analysis 是「分析这个过程」，而不是做分析的人。

normal.en: Think of a watchmaker with a tiny screwdriver: the whole watch is laid out screw by screw.
normal.cn: 想象一位钟表匠拿着小螺丝刀，把整只表一颗螺丝一颗螺丝地摊开。

normal.en: One letter changes the job: analysis is the work, analyst is the worker.
normal.cn: 改一个字母就换了角色：analysis 是活儿，analyst 是干活的人。

normal.en: The plural analyses looks like the singular with an e in place of the second i, so spell it slowly.
normal.cn: 复数 analyses 像是把单数第二个 i 换成 e，拼写时要慢一点。

abstract.en: Analysis is the mind's habit of refusing to swallow a whole thing at once.
abstract.cn: 分析是头脑拒绝把整件事一口吞下的习惯。

abstract.en: Every analysis is a promise that the confusing surface has a structure underneath.
abstract.cn: 每一次分析都在承诺：混乱的表面之下必有一层结构。

abstract.en: To analyze is to trade speed for clarity, and clarity is what the word sells.
abstract.cn: 分析是用速度换清晰，而这个词卖的就是清晰。

examples.en: The team's analysis of the survey data took three weeks.
examples.cn: 团队对调查数据的分析花了三周。

examples.en: A careful analysis can turn a vague worry into a list of concrete problems.
examples.cn: 细致的分析能把模糊的担忧变成一张具体问题的清单。

examples.en: The doctor ordered a blood analysis before prescribing anything.
examples.cn: 医生在开药之前先安排了一次血液化验。

dict_mnemonic.text: 谐音「安娜来析」：安娜来帮你拆开分析，把一团乱麻析成一条一条。

root: 希腊语 ana-（向上、彻底、分开）+ lysis（松开），原义「把整体松开、拆散」。

sensesIntro.en: The word moves from a general act of taking apart, through laboratory and psychological tests, to mathematics and finally to a written examination.
sensesIntro.cn: 这个词从一般的「拆开研究」，经化验与心理治疗，走到数学分支，最后指成篇的评析。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a whole object is loosened and laid out piece by piece until its structure is visible.
core.cn: 核心意象：把一整件东西松开、一块块摊开，直到结构看得见。

branches.en: THE STUDY: the first sense is the general act of separating a subject into parts to understand it.
branches.cn: 研究线：第一个义项是把研究对象分成部分来理解的一般动作。

branches.en: THE LAB: the second sense applies that act to a physical sample and reads its ingredients.
branches.cn: 实验室线：第二个义项把这一动作用于实物样品，读出其中的成分。

branches.en: THE MIND: the third sense turns the same movement inward, toward buried feelings.
branches.cn: 心灵线：第三个义项让同一动作转向内部，朝向被埋藏的情绪。

branches.en: THE FORMULA: the fourth sense narrows the parts to limits and series.
branches.cn: 公式线：第四个义项把被拆分的部分收窄到极限与级数。

branches.en: THE PAGE: the fifth sense writes the general act down for a reader.
branches.cn: 纸面线：第五个义项把一般的拆解动作写下来给读者看。

intro.en: The Greek stem analy- combines with suffixes and prefixes to name the act, the person, the method and the quality.
intro.cn: 希腊词干 analy- 与前后缀组合，分别指称动作、人物、方法与性质。

latinIntro.en: The Latinized stem is analy-, and English builds its family with -sis, -st, -ic, -al and -able.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁化词干为 analy-，英语用 -sis、-st、-ic、-al、-able 等后缀扩展词族。

items.meaning: to break a whole into parts and study them
items.meaningCN: 把整体拆成部分来研究
items.example: Scientists analyze the water before it reaches the city.
items.exampleCN: 科学家在水进入城市之前对它进行分析。

items.example: The analyst flagged three unusual transactions.
items.exampleCN: 分析师标出了三笔异常交易。

items.meaning: working by separating things into parts
items.example: Her analytic approach exposed the weak link.
items.exampleCN: 她的分析式方法暴露了薄弱环节。

items.meaningCN: 基于分析的、显示分析能力的
items.example: The report is long but genuinely analytical.
items.exampleCN: 这份报告虽长，却确有分析深度。

items.meaning: in a manner that separates and examines
items.example: He listened analytically rather than emotionally.
items.exampleCN: 他带着分析的耳朵听，而不是被情绪牵着走。

items.example: The samples are small but still analyzable.
items.exampleCN: 样品虽少，但仍然可以分析。

items.meaning: not yet examined or broken down
items.example: The archive holds boxes of unanalyzed letters.
items.exampleCN: 档案库里还有一箱箱未经分析的信件。

items.meaning: to analyze again, often with new methods
items.example: They reanalyze the old data with a better model.
items.exampleCN: 他们用更好的模型重新分析旧数据。

senses.title: To break something down in order to understand it
senses.titleCN: 分析：拆开复杂事物以理解它
senses.definition: to separate a complex thing into its parts and study how those parts work together
senses.definitionCN: 把复杂事物分成各个部分，并研究这些部分如何共同运作
senses.example: We need to analyze the causes of the failure before blaming anyone.
senses.exampleCN: 在责怪任何人之前，我们需要分析失败的原因。
senses.why: The verb is the action behind analysis: the whole is loosened until the parts can be handled one at a time.
senses.whyCN: 这个动词是 analysis 背后的动作：把整体松开，直到各个部分能被一件一件处理。

senses.title: To test a substance in a laboratory
senses.titleCN: 化验：检测物质的成分
senses.definition: to examine a substance chemically or medically in order to discover what it contains
senses.definitionCN: 用化学或医学方法检测物质，以查明其成分
senses.example: The lab will analyze the soil for heavy metals.
senses.exampleCN: 实验室将检测土壤中的重金属。
senses.why: Laboratory analysis is the same cutting movement applied to matter: the sample is resolved into measurable ingredients.
senses.whyCN: 实验室分析是把同样的「切分」用在物质上：样品被分解成可测量的成分。

senses.title: To treat a patient psychoanalytically
senses.titleCN: 作精神分析：梳理被压抑的心理内容
senses.definition: to treat a person by bringing buried feelings and memories into conscious awareness
senses.definitionCN: 通过把被压抑的情绪与记忆带入意识来治疗一个人
senses.example: The therapist analyzed him twice a week for a year.
senses.exampleCN: 治疗师每周为他做两次精神分析，持续了一年。
senses.why: The mind is treated as a whole that must be loosened: hidden material is separated out and named.
senses.whyCN: 心灵被当作需要松开的整体：隐藏的材料被分离出来并加以命名。

senses.title: To parse a sentence
senses.titleCN: 作语法分析：拆解句子成分
senses.definition: to divide a sentence into its grammatical parts and describe how they fit together
senses.definitionCN: 把句子分成语法成分，并说明它们如何组合
senses.example: The class analyzed the sentence clause by clause.
senses.exampleCN: 全班把这个句子一个从句一个从句地分析。
senses.why: Grammar repeats the same gesture on language: a sentence is cut at its joints so the structure shows.
senses.whyCN: 语法在语言上重复同一个动作：沿句子的关节切开，让结构显形。

senses.title: To process data or code
senses.titleCN: 解析：对数据或代码作计算处理
senses.definition: to examine data or program code systematically, often with a machine, in order to extract meaning or structure
senses.definitionCN: 系统地检查数据或程序代码，常借助机器，以提取意义或结构
senses.example: The software analyzes every message for hidden patterns.
senses.exampleCN: 这个软件会分析每条信息，寻找隐藏的模式。
senses.why: Modern machines perform the old gesture at great speed: they take a stream apart into fields and tokens.
senses.whyCN: 现代机器以极快的速度执行这个古老动作：把数据流拆成字段与标记。

intro.en: Analyze is the verb built beside analysis, and both trace back to the Greek image of loosening something apart.
intro.cn: analyze 是与 analysis 并生的动词，两者都回到希腊语「把某物松开」的意象。

items.en: Analyein meant 'to loosen up, dissolve', from ana- 'up, apart' and lyein 'to loosen'.
items.cn: analyein 意为「松开、溶解」，由 ana-「向上、分开」与 lyein「松开」构成。

items.en: Latin took the noun analysis from Greek; the verb was later formed within the scholarly languages of Europe.
items.cn: 拉丁语从希腊语借入名词 analysis；动词则是在欧洲学术语言中后来形成的。

items.en: French analyser supplied a model for the English verb, which appears in the seventeenth century.
items.cn: 法语 analyser 为英语动词提供了样板，英语动词见于十七世纪。

items.en: British English settled on analyse, with the -ise ending shared by many learned verbs.
items.cn: 英式英语固定为 analyse，采用许多学术动词共有的 -ise 结尾。

items.en: American spelling prefers analyze, with -yze, following a pattern also seen in paralyze.
items.cn: 美式拼写偏好 analyze，用 -yze，这一模式也见于 paralyze。

items.en: The verb now ranges from chemistry to grammar to computing, but each use still cuts a whole into readable parts.
items.cn: 这个动词如今从化学延伸到语法与计算，但每种用法仍在把整体切成可读的部分。

note.en: The look-alike group is the analysis family; the near-meaning group holds verbs of close inspection that differ in method.
note.cn: 形近组是 analysis 词族；近义组收仔细检查类动词，方法各有不同。

entries.definition: The noun naming the act or result of breaking something into parts.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，指把事物分成部分的行为或结果。

entries.definition: A person who analyzes data or samples professionally.
entries.definitionCN: 以分析数据或样品为职业的人。

entries.definition: An adjective for a method that separates things into parts.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，指把事物分成部分的方法。

entries.definition: The adjective meaning skilled at analysis or produced by it.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，义为「善于分析的」或「经分析得出的」。

entries.definition: To look at something closely, often without taking it apart.
entries.definitionCN: 仔细查看某物，通常并不把它拆开。

entries.definition: To cut a body or an argument apart in order to study its parts.
entries.definitionCN: 把身体或论点切开，以研究其各部分。

entries.definition: To explain what something means rather than how it is built.
entries.definitionCN: 解释某物的含义，而非它的构造。

entries.definition: To judge the value or quality of something after examining it.
entries.definitionCN: 在考察之后判断某物的价值或质量。

normalIntro.en: The hooks below link the verb to the noun, to its spelling and to the physical act of cutting something open.
normalIntro.cn: 下面的钩子把这个动词与名词、拼写以及「切开」的实体动作连起来。

normal.en: Analyze is what an analyst does with an analysis: three forms, one job.
normal.cn: analyze 是 analyst 用 analysis 做的事：三个形式，一份工作。

normal.en: The British version swaps the z for an s: analyse looks softer, analyze sharper.
normal.cn: 英式版本把 z 换成 s：analyse 看着更软，analyze 看着更利。

normal.en: Picture a lab technician slicing a sample into thin sections on a glass slide.
normal.cn: 想象实验员把样品切成薄片，放在玻璃载玻片上。

normal.en: The stress is on the second syllable, so the word itself sounds like a decision being made.
normal.cn: 重音在第二音节，读起来像正在下一个判断。

normal.en: You analyze data, a sentence, or a feeling; the verb always wants an object.
normal.cn: 你可以 analyze 数据、句子或情绪；这个动词总要带一个宾语。

abstract.en: To analyze is to refuse the comfort of a first impression.
abstract.cn: 分析就是拒绝第一印象带来的舒适。

abstract.en: Every analysis begins with the admission that the obvious reading is not the whole story.
abstract.cn: 每次分析都始于承认：显而易见的读法并不是全部。

abstract.en: Analysis is patience turned into a method.
abstract.cn: 分析是把耐心变成一种方法。

examples.en: Researchers analyze thousands of samples every month.
examples.cn: 研究人员每个月分析数千份样品。

examples.en: Before you analyze the poem, read it aloud once.
examples.cn: 在分析这首诗之前，先大声读一遍。

examples.en: The program can analyze the logs faster than any person.
examples.cn: 这个程序能比任何人更快地解析日志。

dict_mnemonic.text: 谐音「安拿来试」：安安静静拿过来试一试，一样一样拆开看。

root: 希腊语 ana-（向上、分开）+ lyein（松开），动词义即「把整体松开、拆散」。

sensesIntro.en: The verb starts with general understanding, then specializes into chemical testing, psychotherapy, grammar and machine parsing.
sensesIntro.cn: 这个动词从一般的理解出发，再分化为化验、心理治疗、语法分析与机器解析。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a blade moves through a complex whole so that each layer can be looked at separately.
core.cn: 核心意象：刀刃穿过复杂的整体，让每一层都能被单独查看。

branches.en: THE GENERAL ACT: the first sense is plain understanding by separation.
branches.cn: 一般动作线：第一个义项就是通过分离来理解。

branches.en: THE SAMPLE: the second sense cuts into matter and reads its composition.
branches.cn: 样品线：第二个义项切进物质，读出它的组成。

branches.en: THE MIND: the third sense cuts into memory and feeling.
branches.cn: 心灵线：第三个义项切进记忆与情绪。

branches.en: THE SENTENCE: the fourth sense cuts language at its grammatical joints.
branches.cn: 句子线：第四个义项沿语法关节切开语言。

branches.en: THE MACHINE: the fifth sense makes the cutting automatic and fast.
branches.cn: 机器线：第五个义项让切开变得自动而迅速。

intro.en: The verb and its noun share one Greek stem, and English adds suffixes to mark person, instrument and possibility.
intro.cn: 动词与名词共享一个希腊词干，英语再加后缀标示人物、工具与可能性。

latinIntro.en: The family is built with -sis, -st, -er, -ic, -al and -able around the stem analy-.
latinIntro.cn: 这个词族以 analy- 为核心，用 -sis、-st、-er、-ic、-al、-able 扩展。

items.meaning: the act or result of separating a whole
items.meaningCN: 把整体分开的行为或结果
items.example: The analysis took longer than the experiment.
items.exampleCN: 分析比实验本身花的时间还长。

items.example: She works as a data analyst.
items.exampleCN: 她做数据分析师。

items.meaning: a device or person that analyzes
items.example: The analyzer broke down each frequency.
items.exampleCN: 分析仪把每个频率分解开来。

items.example: He has an analytic mind.
items.exampleCN: 他有一颗分析型的头脑。

items.example: The essay is analytical, not descriptive.
items.exampleCN: 这篇文章是分析性的，不是描述性的。

items.example: She approached the problem analytically.
items.exampleCN: 她以分析的方式处理这个问题。

items.example: The recording is noisy but analyzable.
items.exampleCN: 录音有噪声，但仍可分析。

items.example: Much of the evidence remains unanalyzed.
items.exampleCN: 许多证据仍未得到分析。

definition_zh: 祖先；祖宗；物种祖先；原型；前身
definition_en: a person from whom one is descended, or an early form of a species or thing from which later ones developed
core_image: 家谱树最深处的根，后来的枝干都从那里长出来
scene: 祠堂里，泛黄的族谱被小心展开，老人指着最上面一行名字。The family traced its ancestors back to a fishing village on the coast.
sceneCN: 这里 ancestor 是「家族祖先」（第 1 个义项：血缘上的先人）；句意为这家人把祖先追溯到一个海边渔村。画面里有族谱、供桌与香炉。

pos.zh: 名词：祖先；祖宗；物种祖先；前身

derivatives.zh: 由本词加 -al 构成，义为「祖先的；祖传的」
由本词加 -ry 构成，义为「血统；祖先世系」
由本词加阴性后缀 -ess 构成，义为「女祖先」
ancestral 加 -ly 构成，义为「按祖传方式；世袭地」

senses.title: A family forebear
senses.titleCN: 家族祖先：血缘上的先人
senses.definition: a person in one's family line who lived before one's grandparents, especially a distant forebear
senses.definitionCN: 家族血脉中早于祖辈的人，尤指年代久远的先人
senses.example: Her ancestors came to the island three centuries ago.
senses.exampleCN: 她的祖先在三个世纪前来到这座岛。
senses.why: Latin antecessor meant 'one who goes before'; an ancestor is simply the person who walked ahead of you in the family line.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁语 antecessor 意为「走在前面的那个人」，祖先就是在家族血脉中先你而行的人。

senses.title: An earlier species or type
senses.titleCN: 物种祖先：演化上的早期类型
senses.definition: an earlier species, form, or organism from which a later species is descended
senses.definitionCN: 后来的物种由之演化而来的更早物种、形态或生物
senses.example: The fossil is believed to be an ancestor of modern birds.
senses.exampleCN: 这块化石被认为是现代鸟类的祖先。
senses.why: Evolution borrows the family tree: the older branch is literally the line that came before the newer one.
senses.whyCN: 演化论借用了家谱树：较老的分支就是先于较新分支出现的那条线。

senses.title: An early form of a thing
senses.titleCN: 前身：事物的早期雏形
senses.definition: an early version or model of something that later developed into its present form
senses.definitionCN: 后来发展成现今形态的事物的早期版本或雏形
senses.example: The adding machine was an ancestor of the computer.
senses.exampleCN: 加法机是计算机的前身。
senses.why: Objects are given genealogies too: the clumsy early model is the ancestor of the sleek machine that replaced it.
senses.whyCN: 器物也被赋予家谱：笨拙的早期型号就是取代它的精巧机器之前身。

senses.title: A higher node in a tree structure
senses.titleCN: 上级节点：计算机树结构中的前辈
senses.definition: in computing, a node in a tree structure that lies on the path above a given node
senses.definitionCN: 计算机树结构中位于某一节点上方路径上的节点
senses.example: Each file belongs to a folder that is its ancestor in the tree.
senses.exampleCN: 每个文件都属于一个文件夹，该文件夹就是它在树中的上级节点。
senses.why: The family-tree image survives in data structures: nodes have parents, and the parents above them are ancestors.
senses.whyCN: 家谱的意象在数据结构中保留下来：节点有父节点，而父节点之上的那些节点就是祖先。

intro.en: Ancestor is a Latin word about walking ahead, carried into English by way of Old French.
intro.cn: ancestor 是一个关于「走在前面」的拉丁词，经古法语进入英语。

items.en: The preposition ante meant 'before, in front of', and it still appears in English words such as antebellum.
items.cn: 介词 ante 意为「在……之前、在前面」，至今仍见于 antebellum 等英语词中。

items.en: Cedere meant 'to go, yield', and the two parts made antecedere, 'to go before'.
items.cn: cedere 意为「走、让出」，两部分合成 antecedere，即「走在前面」。

items.en: Antecessor named the person who went before, a predecessor. In law it could also mean one who precedes another in an office.
items.cn: antecessor 指走在前面的人，即前任；在法律语境中也可指职位上的前任。

items.en: Old French reshaped the word as ancestre and used it for a forebear in one's family.
items.cn: 古法语把词形改成 ancestre，用来指家族中的先人。

items.en: English borrowed the word in the thirteenth century. The spelling settled as ancestor later, and exact first dates are uncertain.
items.cn: 英语在十三世纪借入这个词，拼写后来固定为 ancestor；确切首见年代不确定。

items.en: Biology and computing extended the word from people to species and to nodes, keeping the same direction of descent.
items.cn: 生物学与计算机把这个词从人扩展到物种与节点，但「向下传承」的方向始终不变。

note.en: The look-alike group is the ancestry family; the near-meaning group names people or things that came before.
note.cn: 形近组是 ancestry 词族；近义组指先于某人或某物出现的人与物。

entries.definition: The whole line of forebears, or the origin of a family.
entries.definitionCN: 指祖先的整条世系，或一个家族的血统来源。

entries.definition: An adjective meaning belonging to or inherited from ancestors.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，义为「祖先的、祖传的」。

entries.definition: A female ancestor, formed with the feminine suffix.
entries.definitionCN: 由阴性后缀构成的名词，义为「女祖先」。

entries.definition: A male ancestor, often used of a nation's early people.
entries.definitionCN: 男性祖先，常用于一个民族早期的先人。

entries.definition: The person who held a post or came before another in time.
entries.definitionCN: 职位上的前任，或时间上先于某人的人。

entries.definition: A direct forebear or the original source of a line.
entries.definitionCN: 直系祖先，或某一世系的最初源头。

entries.definition: A more formal word for an ancestor.
entries.definitionCN: 较为正式的「祖先」说法。

normalIntro.en: These hooks connect the word to the family tree, to its Latin direction 'before', and to its sound.
normalIntro.cn: 下面几个钩子把这个词与家谱树、拉丁语「在前」的方向以及读音连起来。

normal.en: The root ante- means before, so an ancestor is the one who went before you.
normal.cn: 词根 ante- 意为「在前」，所以 ancestor 就是先你而行的人。

normal.en: Say 'AN-ses-ter': the heavy first beat sounds like the oldest name at the top of the page.
normal.cn: 读作「AN-塞斯-特」，第一拍最重，像族谱最上面那个最老的名字。

normal.en: Picture a tree: roots underground, and you standing at the tip of a branch.
normal.cn: 想象一棵树：根在地下，而你站在某一根枝条的末端。

normal.en: The ending -or often marks a person, as in actor and doctor, and here it marks a person in the family line.
normal.cn: 结尾 -or 常标示人，如 actor、doctor，这里标示家族血脉中的一个人。

normal.en: One ancestor, many ancestors: the plural simply adds an s to the long word.
normal.cn: 一个 ancestor，许多 ancestors：复数只是在这个长词后加 s。

abstract.en: An ancestor is a name you inherit without having met the person.
abstract.cn: 祖先是一个你继承了、却从未见过本人的名字。

abstract.en: Every ancestor is proof that the present was built on someone else's choices.
abstract.cn: 每一位祖先都证明：现在建立在别人的选择之上。

abstract.en: To look for ancestors is to look for the earliest version of yourself.
abstract.cn: 寻找祖先，就是寻找你自己最早的版本。

examples.en: My ancestors left the mountains in search of work.
examples.cn: 我的祖先为了谋生离开了山区。

examples.en: The two species share a common ancestor.
examples.cn: 这两个物种拥有共同祖先。

examples.en: This old engine is the ancestor of every jet turbine.
examples.cn: 这台老发动机是每一台喷气涡轮的前身。

dict_mnemonic.text: 谐音「俺塞斯特」：俺家老祖宗塞在斯特拉大山里，往上数都是他们。

root: 拉丁语 ante（在前）+ cedere（走），antecessor 即「走在前面的人」，后经古法语作 ancestre。

sensesIntro.en: The word begins with family forebears and extends to species, to early models of things, and to higher nodes in data trees.
sensesIntro.cn: 这个词从家族先人出发，扩展到物种、器物的早期型号，以及数据树中的上级节点。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a deep root at the bottom of a family tree, feeding every branch above it.
core.cn: 核心意象：家谱树最底部的一条深根，供养着上方每一根枝条。

branches.en: THE FAMILY: the first sense is the human forebear in one's own line.
branches.cn: 家族线：第一个义项是自家血脉中的先人。

branches.en: THE SPECIES: the second sense moves the same relation to living kinds.
branches.cn: 物种线：第二个义项把同一关系移到生物种类上。

branches.en: THE MACHINE: the third sense gives objects a genealogy of their own.
branches.cn: 器物线：第三个义项让器物也拥有自己的家谱。

branches.en: THE TREE: the fourth sense keeps the family image inside a data structure.
branches.cn: 树结构线：第四个义项把家族意象保留在数据结构里。

branches.en: THE DIRECTION: both the species and the model point backward, toward what came first.
branches.cn: 方向线：物种义与雏形义都向后指，指向最先出现的东西。

intro.en: The family is built on the Latin stem ancestr-, with suffixes for the line, the adjective and the female forebear.
intro.cn: 这个词族建立在拉丁词干 ancestr- 上，用后缀构成世系、形容词与女祖先。

latinIntro.en: Latin ante- 'before' plus cedere 'go' produced antecessor; English reshaped it and added -ry, -al and -ess.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 ante-「在前」加 cedere「走」构成 antecessor，英语改写后加 -ry、-al、-ess。

items.meaning: the line of ancestors behind a person
items.meaningCN: 一个人背后的祖先世系
items.example: She researched her ancestry for years.
items.exampleCN: 她研究自己的祖先世系多年。

items.example: They returned to the ancestral village.
items.exampleCN: 他们回到了祖籍村庄。

items.meaning: in a manner handed down from ancestors
items.example: The land was ancestrally held.
items.exampleCN: 这块土地是祖上传下的。

items.example: The ancestress of the clan is honored each spring.
items.exampleCN: 这个宗族的女祖先每年春天受到祭拜。

items.meaning: a shared forebear of two lines
items.example: Both breeds descend from a common ancestor.
items.exampleCN: 这两个品种都源自一个共同祖先。

items.meaning: an ancestor in the straight family line
items.example: His direct ancestor arrived in the year the town was founded.
items.exampleCN: 他的直系祖先在小镇建立那年来到这里。

items.meaning: the practice of honoring dead forebears
items.example: Ancestor worship shaped the festival calendar.
items.exampleCN: 祭祖习俗塑造了节日的安排。

items.meaning: the house or place long held by a family
items.meaningCN: 家族世代居住的老宅或故土
items.example: They restored the ancestral home stone by stone.
items.exampleCN: 他们一块石头一块石头地修复祖宅。

definition_zh: 锚；锚点；（新闻）主播；支柱；抛锚；使固定
definition_en: a heavy device dropped from a boat to hold it in place, or something that gives stability and holds other things together
core_image: 一只沉入水底的铁爪，把漂动的船牢牢钉在一处
scene: 风暴逼近港湾，货轮在浪里剧烈摇晃，船长抓起对讲机下令。The captain ordered the crew to drop anchor before the storm hit.
sceneCN: 这里 anchor 是「锚」（第 1 个义项：使船固定不动的重物）；句意为船长下令船员在风暴来临前抛锚。画面里有货轮、铁链与翻涌的海水。

pos.zh: 名词：锚；锚点；主播；支柱
动词：抛锚；使固定；主持（节目）

derivatives.zh: 由本词加 -age 构成，义为「锚地；停泊处」
由本词与 man 复合，义为「男主播；压阵者」
由本词与 woman 复合，义为「女主播」
由本词与 person 复合，义为「主播（中性说法）」
由本词加 -less 构成，义为「无锚的；无依靠的」

senses.title: The heavy device that holds a ship
senses.titleCN: 船锚：把船固定在水中
senses.definition: a heavy metal device with hooks, dropped to the seabed on a chain to keep a boat from drifting
senses.definitionCN: 带钩的重金属装置，用链条沉到海底，使船不漂走
senses.example: The old fishing boat rode at anchor all night.
senses.exampleCN: 那艘旧渔船整夜停泊在锚上。
senses.why: The Greek word named the hook itself; the physical hook is still the picture behind every figurative use.
senses.whyCN: 希腊语原指那个钩子；这个实体的钩子至今仍是所有比喻用法背后的画面。

senses.title: A news presenter
senses.titleCN: 新闻主播：节目的固定主持者
senses.definition: a person who presents a broadcast news programme and holds it together from the studio
senses.definitionCN: 在演播室播报新闻、把整档节目串联起来的人
senses.example: The anchor stayed calm while the reports came in.
senses.exampleCN: 消息不断传来时，主播始终保持镇定。
senses.why: The presenter is the fixed point the broadcast hangs on, just as a ship hangs on its anchor.
senses.whyCN: 主播是整档节目所系住的固定点，正如船系在锚上。

senses.title: A mainstay
senses.titleCN: 支柱：让整体稳定的中坚
senses.definition: a person or thing that provides stability and holds a group or system together
senses.definitionCN: 提供稳定性、把一个群体或体系维系在一起的人或物
senses.example: She was the anchor of the department during the crisis.
senses.exampleCN: 危机期间，她是整个部门的支柱。
senses.why: A team that might drift apart is imagined as a ship; the reliable member is what keeps it from drifting.
senses.whyCN: 可能离散的团队被想象成一艘船；可靠的那名成员就是防止它漂走的东西。

senses.title: A fixed reference point
senses.titleCN: 锚点：网页与图形中的固定参照
senses.definition: a fixed point in a document, image, or coordinate system that other things are attached to or measured from
senses.definitionCN: 文档、图像或坐标体系中供其他对象附着或据以测量的固定点
senses.example: The link jumps to an anchor halfway down the page.
senses.exampleCN: 这个链接会跳转到页面中部的锚点。
senses.why: The hook becomes a coordinate: something fixed that everything else can be tied to.
senses.whyCN: 钩子变成了坐标：一个固定的点，别的东西都可以系在它上面。

senses.title: To moor a boat
senses.titleCN: 抛锚；停泊
senses.definition: to drop the anchor and hold a boat in one place, or to come to rest in a harbour
senses.definitionCN: 抛下锚使船停在某处，或在港湾停泊
senses.example: We anchored in a quiet bay until the wind dropped.
senses.exampleCN: 我们在一处安静的海湾抛锚，直到风停下来。
senses.why: The noun turns into the act: the hook is let go, and the movement of the boat stops.
senses.whyCN: 名词变成动作：钩子被放下，船的移动随之停止。

senses.title: To fix something firmly
senses.titleCN: 使固定；系牢
senses.definition: to fasten something firmly so that it cannot move or shift
senses.definitionCN: 把某物牢牢固定，使其不能移动或错位
senses.example: The shelves were anchored to the wall with steel bolts.
senses.exampleCN: 架子用钢螺栓固定在墙上。
senses.why: Any object that must not drift is treated like a boat: something strong is driven in and holds it.
senses.whyCN: 任何不能漂移的东西都被当作船来处理：钉入一个坚固之物把它拉住。

senses.title: To present a broadcast
senses.titleCN: 主持（节目）：串联整场播出
senses.definition: to act as the main presenter of a broadcast, keeping its parts connected and on time
senses.definitionCN: 担任播出节目的主要主持人，使各部分衔接并按时进行
senses.example: He anchored the evening news for twenty years.
senses.exampleCN: 他主持晚间新闻长达二十年。
senses.why: The presenter holds the programme the way an anchor holds a ship: one fixed point around which everything moves.
senses.whyCN: 主持人稳住节目的方式就像锚稳住船：一个固定点，四周的一切围绕它运转。

intro.en: Anchor is a Greek word for a hook that entered English through Latin and Old English, and its spelling was later corrected back toward Latin.
intro.cn: anchor 是希腊语中表示「钩子」的词，经拉丁语与古英语进入英语，拼写后来又被拉回拉丁语形式。

items.en: Ankyra meant 'anchor', and it is related to ankylos, 'bent, hooked'. The shape gave the name.
items.cn: ankyra 意为「锚」，与 ankylos「弯曲的、带钩的」相关；是形状给了它这个名字。

items.en: Latin borrowed the word as ancora, keeping both the object and its hook-like shape.
items.cn: 拉丁语借入作 ancora，既保留了实物，也保留了钩状的形状。

items.en: Old English took the word from Latin as ancor, and it appears in religious and nautical writing.
items.cn: 古英语从拉丁语借入 ancor，见于宗教与航海文本。

items.en: Middle English spellings included anker and ankre, showing how the sound had shifted.
items.cn: 中古英语拼写有 anker、ankre 等，显示读音已经变化。

items.en: Sixteenth-century writers restored the Latin-looking ch, producing the modern anchor.
items.cn: 十六世纪的作者恢复了看似拉丁语的 ch，形成现代拼写 anchor。

items.en: Broadcasting gave the word a new human sense, and computing gave it a new kind of fixed point.
items.cn: 广播业赋予它新的人物义，计算机则赋予它一种新的固定点含义。

note.en: The look-alike group is the anchor family; the near-meaning group holds words for mooring, holding and stability.
note.cn: 形近组是 anchor 词族；近义组收停泊、固定与稳定类词。

entries.definition: A place where ships may anchor, or the act of anchoring.
entries.definitionCN: 可供船只停泊的锚地，或抛锚的行为。

entries.definition: A male news presenter or the person who holds a team together.
entries.definitionCN: 男新闻主播，或稳住一支队伍的人。

entries.definition: A female news presenter.
entries.definitionCN: 女新闻主播。

entries.definition: To tie a boat to a fixed point on shore or on the seabed.
entries.definitionCN: 把船系在岸上或海底的固定点。

entries.definition: A place where a ship lies when it is tied up.
entries.definitionCN: 船系泊时所占的位置。

entries.definition: The chief support of a group or system.
entries.definitionCN: 一个群体或体系的主要支撑。

entries.definition: A person who introduces and hosts a programme.
entries.definitionCN: 介绍并主持节目的人。

normalIntro.en: These hooks tie the word to its shape, its spelling history and the idea of one fixed point.
normalIntro.cn: 下面几个钩子把这个词与它的形状、拼写历史以及「一个固定点」的观念绑在一起。

normal.en: The ch in anchor is a piece of spelling history: older English wrote anker.
normal.cn: anchor 里的 ch 是拼写史的痕迹：更早的英语写作 anker。

normal.en: Picture the hook biting into the seabed while the boat swings around above it.
normal.cn: 想象钩子咬进海底，而船在上方绕着它摆荡。

normal.en: An anchor holds a ship; an anchor holds a news programme; the same job in two worlds.
normal.cn: anchor 稳住一艘船，也稳住一档新闻节目；两个世界里的同一份工作。

normal.en: The stress is on the first syllable, 'AN-chor', short and heavy like the object itself.
normal.cn: 重音在第一音节「AN-克」，又短又重，就像那个铁家伙。

normal.en: Drop anchor and weigh anchor are opposite actions: one stops the ship, one lets it go.
normal.cn: drop anchor 与 weigh anchor 是相反动作：一个让船停下，一个放船离开。

abstract.en: An anchor is any fixed point that makes movement safe.
abstract.cn: 锚就是任何让运动变得安全的固定点。

abstract.en: People need anchors as much as ships do, and often they are other people.
abstract.cn: 人和船一样需要锚，而那个锚常常是别人。

abstract.en: To anchor something is to decide that it will not be allowed to drift.
abstract.cn: 把某物锚定，就是决定不许它漂走。

examples.en: The ship dropped anchor just outside the harbour.
examples.cn: 船在港湾外不远处抛锚。

examples.en: Use a strong bolt to anchor the shelf to the wall.
examples.cn: 用结实的螺栓把架子固定在墙上。

examples.en: She anchored the morning show for a decade.
examples.cn: 她主持早间节目长达十年。

dict_mnemonic.text: 谐音「安可」：船到岸了，大家喊「安可」，抛下锚就不再漂走。

root: 希腊语 ankyra（锚，与 ankylos「弯曲带钩」相关）→ 拉丁语 ancora → 古英语 ancor。

sensesIntro.en: A physical hook for ships grows into a presenter, a mainstay, a reference point, and finally into verbs of mooring, fixing and hosting.
sensesIntro.cn: 船用的实体钩子，逐步引申为主播、支柱、参照点，最后成为停泊、固定与主持的动词。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: an iron hook bites into the seabed and stops a drifting hull.
core.cn: 核心意象：铁钩咬进海底，让漂动的船身停住。

branches.en: THE OBJECT: the first sense is the literal iron device.
branches.cn: 实物线：第一个义项就是字面上的铁制装置。

branches.en: THE STUDIO: the second sense makes a person the fixed point of a broadcast.
branches.cn: 演播室线：第二个义项把人变成一档播出的固定点。

branches.en: THE SUPPORT: the third sense makes a person or thing the stability of a group.
branches.cn: 支撑线：第三个义项让人或物成为群体的稳定来源。

branches.en: THE REFERENCE: the fourth sense turns the hook into a coordinate others attach to.
branches.cn: 参照线：第四个义项把钩子变成别的对象可附着的坐标。

branches.en: THE ACTIONS: the last three senses turn the object into mooring, fixing and hosting.
branches.cn: 动作线：后三个义项把实物转为停泊、固定与主持。

intro.en: The family joins anchor to suffixes and nouns to name places, people, and the lack of support.
intro.cn: 这个词族把 anchor 与后缀及名词组合，指称地点、人物与「失去支撑」。

latinIntro.en: From Latin ancora and Old English ancor, English forms anchorage with -age and compounds with man, woman and person.
latinIntro.cn: 由拉丁语 ancora 与古英语 ancor，英语用 -age 构成 anchorage，并与 man、woman、person 组成复合词。

items.meaning: a place for anchoring, or the state of being anchored
items.example: The bay offers safe anchorage in any weather.
items.exampleCN: 这个海湾在任何天气下都能安全停泊。

items.meaning: a male presenter or the steady member of a team
items.meaningCN: 男主播，或队伍中稳住局面的人
items.example: The anchorman kept the debate from falling apart.
items.exampleCN: 那位主播没让辩论失控。

items.example: The anchorwoman opened the programme with a calm smile.
items.exampleCN: 女主播带着平静的微笑开场。

items.meaning: a gender-neutral word for a presenter
items.example: The station hired a new anchorperson.
items.exampleCN: 电视台新聘了一位主播。

items.meaning: without an anchor or without support
items.example: The anchorless boat drifted into the fog.
items.exampleCN: 失去锚的船漂进了雾里。

items.meaning: to anchor again or in a new place
items.meaningCN: 重新抛锚或改系到新位置
items.example: They reanchor the buoy every spring.
items.exampleCN: 他们每年春天重新固定浮标。

items.meaning: to let the anchor down and stop
items.example: We drop anchor outside the reef.
items.exampleCN: 我们在礁石外抛锚。

items.meaning: to lift the anchor and prepare to sail
items.example: They weigh anchor at first light.
items.exampleCN: 他们天亮时起锚。

definition_zh: 古代的；古老的；年迈的；（名词）古人
definition_en: belonging to a period of history long past, or extremely old
core_image: 石柱上被风磨平的花纹，时间在上面留下了厚厚一层灰
scene: 博物馆的玻璃柜里，一只陶罐的釉面已经裂成细密的网。The guide explained that the ancient jar was made by hand.
sceneCN: 这里 ancient 是「古代的、古老的」（第 1 个义项：属于久远历史的）；句意为讲解员说明这只古老的陶罐是手工制作的。画面里有陶罐、展柜与说明牌。

pos.zh: 形容词：古代的；古老的；年迈的
名词：古人（尤指古代民族）

derivatives.zh: 由本词加 -ly 构成，义为「在古代；很久以前」
由本词加 -ness 构成，义为「古老；年代久远」
由本词加 -ry 构成，义为「古旧的事物；古老的风尚」（罕用）

senses.title: Belonging to a far past civilization
senses.titleCN: 古代的：属于久远历史时期
senses.definition: belonging to the distant past, especially to civilizations such as those of Greece, Rome or Egypt
senses.definitionCN: 属于遥远的过去，尤指希腊、罗马、埃及等文明所在的时期
senses.example: Ancient Egypt built pyramids that still stand today.
senses.exampleCN: 古埃及建造的金字塔至今仍然矗立。
senses.why: Latin ante meant 'before'; ancient marks the part of history that lies furthest before us.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁语 ante 意为「在……之前」，ancient 标出的正是离我们最远的那段历史。

senses.title: Extremely old
senses.titleCN: 古老的：年代久远的事物
senses.definition: having existed for a very long time, often used of objects, buildings or trees
senses.definitionCN: 已经存在很久，常用于物件、建筑或树木
senses.example: An ancient oak stands at the corner of the field.
senses.exampleCN: 田角立着一棵古老的橡树。
senses.why: The historical sense is applied to single things: anything that has outlived many generations feels ancient.
senses.whyCN: 历史义被用在单个事物上：任何活过许多代人的东西，都让人觉得古老。

senses.title: Very old, humorously of a person
senses.titleCN: 年迈的：口语中略带戏谑
senses.definition: extremely old, used humorously or affectionately about a person
senses.definitionCN: 年纪很大，带戏谑或亲昵意味地用于人
senses.example: My ancient neighbour still walks to the market every day.
senses.exampleCN: 我那位年迈的邻居每天仍走路去市场。
senses.why: Calling a living person ancient is a gentle joke: the word's huge stretch of time is borrowed for a single life.
senses.whyCN: 把活人称作 ancient 是一种温和的玩笑：词里那段漫长的历史被借来形容一个人的一生。

senses.title: The people of ancient times
senses.titleCN: 古人：古代的民族
senses.definition: the people who lived in ancient times, considered as a group
senses.definitionCN: 生活在古代的人，作为一个群体来看待
senses.example: The ancients mapped the stars without telescopes.
senses.exampleCN: 古人在没有望远镜的情况下绘制了星图。
senses.why: The adjective becomes a noun for the people it describes, a common English habit with age words.
senses.whyCN: 形容词转作名词，指它所描述的那群人，这是英语里年龄类词汇常见的用法。

intro.en: Ancient comes from Latin words for 'before', and its spelling was reshaped by French and by later English writers.
intro.cn: ancient 来自拉丁语中表示「在前」的词，拼写又经法语与后世英语作者改写。

items.en: Ante meant 'before, in front of'. From it Latin built antiquus, 'old, former'.
items.cn: ante 意为「在……之前、在前面」，拉丁语由它构成 antiquus，即「旧的、从前的」。

items.en: Antiquus described what belonged to earlier times, and it also gave English antique and antiquated.
items.cn: antiquus 描述属于更早时代的事物，也生出英语的 antique 与 antiquated。

items.en: Old French reduced the word to ancien, which English borrowed with the meaning 'old, former'.
items.cn: 古法语把词形简化为 ancien，英语借入时意为「旧的、从前的」。

items.en: Middle English spellings such as auncien show the French shape before the modern word settled.
items.cn: 中古英语拼写如 auncien 显示了现代词形固定之前的法语形态。

items.en: Later writers inserted the t, probably by association with Latin antiquus, producing ancient.
items.cn: 后来的作者插入了 t，可能与拉丁语 antiquus 的联想有关，于是形成 ancient。

items.en: The word now covers civilizations, old objects and, informally, very old people.
items.cn: 这个词如今覆盖古代文明、古老物件，以及口语中形容很老的人。

note.en: The look-alike group holds words of the same Latin family; the near-meaning group holds words for age, distance in time and antiquity.
note.cn: 形近组收同一拉丁词族的词；近义组收表示年岁、时间距离与古旧程度的词。

entries.definition: An old and valuable object, or an adjective meaning belonging to an earlier period.
entries.definitionCN: 古老而值钱的物件，或形容词「旧时的、古董的」。

entries.definition: Old-fashioned and no longer useful, often said of ideas or machines.
entries.definitionCN: 过时的、不再有用的，常用于观念或机器。

entries.definition: The ancient past, or the quality of being very old.
entries.definitionCN: 指古代，或「古老」这一性质。

entries.definition: The general word for having lived or existed a long time.
entries.definitionCN: 表示「活过或存在了很久」的通用词。

entries.definition: Old, especially of a person, and often neutral or respectful.
entries.definitionCN: 年老的，尤用于人，常为中性或尊敬的说法。

entries.definition: Belonging to an earlier period and no longer in ordinary use.
entries.definitionCN: 属于更早时期、已不在日常使用中的。

entries.definition: Of the earliest ages of the world, far older than human history.
entries.definitionCN: 指世界最古老的年代，比人类历史还要久远。

normalIntro.en: These hooks link the word to its Latin 'before', to its respelled t, and to the picture of worn stone.
normalIntro.cn: 下面几个钩子把这个词与拉丁语「在前」、后来插入的 t，以及被磨旧的石头画面连起来。

normal.en: The hidden ante- means before, so ancient things sit before us on the timeline.
normal.cn: 隐藏的 ante- 意为「在前」，所以 ancient 的东西在时间线上位于我们之前。

normal.en: The t in ancient was added later, like a stone marker planted in the word.
normal.cn: ancient 里的 t 是后来加上的，像插在词里的一块石碑。

normal.en: Say it 'AIN-shunt': the soft ending sounds like worn stone rather than a hard break.
normal.cn: 读作「AIN-申特」，收尾很软，像被磨平的石头而不是硬邦邦的断口。

normal.en: Ancient history, ancient ruins, ancient trees: the word always stretches time backward.
normal.cn: 古代史、古代遗迹、古树：这个词总把时间往后拉。

normal.en: The noun the ancients simply capitalizes the people the adjective describes.
normal.cn: 名词 the ancients 只是把形容词所描述的那群古人提出来。

abstract.en: Ancient is a word for the distance that makes a thing hard to imagine.
abstract.cn: ancient 描述的是那种让人难以想象的遥远。

abstract.en: What is ancient survives by being ignored as well as by being valued.
abstract.cn: 古老之物能留存下来，既因为被珍视，也因为被忽略。

abstract.en: Every ancient thing was once brand new, which is the quiet joke inside the word.
abstract.cn: 每件古老的东西都曾是崭新的，这是这个词里安静的笑话。

examples.en: Ancient Greek plays are still performed today.
examples.cn: 古希腊戏剧至今仍在上演。

examples.en: They found an ancient coin buried under the field.
examples.cn: 他们在田地下发现了一枚古币。

examples.en: The temple is ancient, but its roof was repaired last year.
examples.cn: 这座庙很古老，但屋顶去年修过。

dict_mnemonic.text: 谐音「俺婶特」：俺婶特爱讲古，一开口就是几百年前的事。

root: 拉丁语 ante（在前）+ -quus，构成 antiquus（旧的、从前的），经古法语 ancien 进入英语。

sensesIntro.en: The word starts with whole civilizations, narrows to very old objects, then to a humorous description of age, and finally becomes a noun for ancient peoples.
sensesIntro.cn: 这个词从整个古代文明出发，收窄到很老的物件，再到戏谑地形容年纪，最后成为指古人的名词。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a stone surface worn smooth by centuries, with the marks of hands still faintly visible.
core.cn: 核心意象：被数百年磨平的石面，手工的痕迹仍隐约可见。

branches.en: THE CIVILIZATION: the first sense covers whole ancient cultures.
branches.cn: 文明线：第一个义项覆盖整个古代文化。

branches.en: THE OBJECT: the second sense applies the same age to a single thing.
branches.cn: 物件线：第二个义项把同样的年岁用在单个事物上。

branches.en: THE PERSON: the third sense lends the word to one living person as a joke.
branches.cn: 人物线：第三个义项把词借给一个活人，带着玩笑意味。

branches.en: THE NOUN: the fourth sense turns the adjective into a name for ancient peoples.
branches.cn: 名词线：第四个义项把形容词变成古代民族的名称。

branches.en: THE COMMON THREAD: both old objects and old people simply carry more time than usual.
branches.cn: 共同线：老物件与老人一样，都只是比寻常多带了时间。

intro.en: The Latin family around ante- produces adjectives, nouns and adverbs of age and precedence.
intro.cn: 以 ante- 为核心的拉丁词族，生成表示年岁与先后的形容词、名词和副词。

latinIntro.en: Latin antiquus gave English antique, antiquated and antiquity, while ancient itself came through French.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 antiquus 生出英语的 antique、antiquated、antiquity，而 ancient 本身经法语而来。

items.example: The valley was anciently covered by forest.
items.exampleCN: 这个山谷在古代被森林覆盖。

items.example: The stone's ancientness was obvious at a touch.
items.exampleCN: 一摸就能感到这块石头的古老。

items.meaning: an object from an earlier period
items.example: She collects antique clocks.
items.exampleCN: 她收藏古董钟。

items.example: The factory still uses antiquated machinery.
items.exampleCN: 这家工厂仍在使用过时的机器。

items.meaning: the ancient past or great age
items.example: The vase is valued for its antiquity.
items.exampleCN: 这只花瓶因年代久远而珍贵。

items.meaning: a person who studies old objects
items.example: An antiquarian catalogued the finds.
items.exampleCN: 一位古物研究者给这些发现编了目。

items.example: He teaches ancient history at the university.
items.exampleCN: 他在大学教古代史。

items.meaning: remains of buildings from the distant past
items.example: Tourists walked among the ancient ruins.
items.exampleCN: 游客们在古代遗迹间行走。

definition_zh: 和；与；并且；然后；那么；加
definition_en: a conjunction used to join words, phrases or clauses, or to show that one action follows another
core_image: 两只手把两样东西并排放在一起，中间用一根细线连住
scene: 壁炉前的猫蜷成一团，眼皮越来越沉。The cat sat on the warm mat and fell asleep.
sceneCN: 这里 and 是「并且、然后」（第 2 个义项：连接先后发生的动作）；句意为猫坐在暖垫上，然后睡着了。画面里有壁炉、猫与毛毯。

pos.zh: 连词：和；并且；然后；那么

collocations.zh: 以及所有相关的东西（口语）

derivatives.zh: 同源词，与 and 同出古英语的「第二、另一个」义，义为「其他的」
由 other 加 -wise 构成，义为「否则；在其他方面」
由 and 与 or 合成的固定形式，义为「和（或）……两者皆可」

senses.title: Joining words of the same kind
senses.titleCN: 并列：连接同类词语
senses.definition: used to join two words, phrases or clauses of the same kind, so that both are included
senses.definitionCN: 用来连接两个同类词语、短语或从句，表示两者都包括在内
senses.example: She bought bread and milk on the way home.
senses.exampleCN: 她在回家路上买了面包和牛奶。
senses.why: The oldest job of the word is simply to put two things side by side and say: take both.
senses.whyCN: 这个词最古老的工作就是把两样东西并排放好，说：两样都要。

senses.title: Showing a sequence of actions
senses.titleCN: 顺承：连接先后的动作
senses.definition: used between two actions to show that the second happens after the first
senses.definitionCN: 用在两个动作之间，表示第二个动作发生在第一个之后
senses.example: He opened the window and let in the cool air.
senses.exampleCN: 他打开窗户，让凉空气进来。
senses.why: Two events placed in one line are read in order, so the joining word quietly becomes 'then'.
senses.whyCN: 两个事件被放进同一条线，读者便按顺序理解，于是这个连接词悄悄变成了「然后」。

senses.title: Result or condition after a command
senses.titleCN: 结果：命令句之后引出后果
senses.definition: used after an imperative to mean 'and if you do that, this will follow'
senses.definitionCN: 用在祈使句之后，表示「如果你那样做，就会出现下面的结果」
senses.example: Work hard and you will pass the exam.
senses.exampleCN: 努力学习，你就能通过考试。
senses.why: The two halves are still joined, but now the first is a condition and the second is what it produces.
senses.whyCN: 两半仍然相连，只是此时前半是条件，后半是它带来的结果。

senses.title: Addition in numbers
senses.titleCN: 相加：数字之间的加
senses.definition: used between numbers to mean that they are added together
senses.definitionCN: 用在数字之间，表示把它们相加
senses.example: Two and three makes five.
senses.exampleCN: 二加三等于五。
senses.why: Arithmetic keeps the simplest sense of the word: this quantity plus that quantity, placed in one sum.
senses.whyCN: 算术保留了这个词最简单的意思：这个量加上那个量，放在同一个和里。

intro.en: And is one of the oldest words in English, and its shape has barely changed in a thousand years.
intro.cn: and 是英语中最古老的词之一，一千年来它的形态几乎没有变化。

items.en: Old English used and and ond, and the word already joined words and clauses in the modern way.
items.cn: 古英语用 and 与 ond，当时这个词已经以现代方式连接词语和从句。

items.en: The reconstructed Germanic form is anda, a general connective shared by the Germanic languages.
items.cn: 重构的日耳曼语形式为 anda，是日耳曼诸语共有的通用连接词。

items.en: German und and Dutch en are cousins of the English word, all doing the same joining work.
items.cn: 德语 und 与荷兰语 en 都是英语这个词的表亲，做着同样的连接工作。

items.en: Middle English kept the form and, and the spelling became fixed earlier than in most function words.
items.cn: 中古英语保留了 and 这一形式，拼写比多数功能词更早固定。

items.en: The word now carries listing, sequence, result and arithmetic, all from the single act of joining.
items.cn: 这个词如今承担列举、顺承、结果与加法，全都来自「连接」这一个动作。

note.en: The look-alike group gathers short words that rhyme or nearly rhyme with and; the near-meaning group gathers other connectives and adders.
note.cn: 形近组收与 and 押韵或近韵的短词；近义组收其他连接词与表示添加的词。

entries.definition: A group of musicians, or a strip used to bind things together.
entries.definitionCN: 指乐队，或用来捆扎东西的带子。

entries.definition: The part of the body at the end of the arm.
entries.definitionCN: 手臂末端的手。

entries.definition: The solid surface of the earth, or to come down to it.
entries.definitionCN: 指陆地，或降落着地。

entries.definition: Tiny grains of rock found on beaches and in deserts.
entries.definitionCN: 海滩与沙漠中细小的岩石颗粒。

entries.definition: A word for addition, used in sums and in added remarks.
entries.definitionCN: 表示添加的词，用于加法与补充说明。

entries.definition: An adverb meaning in addition, used to add a further point.
entries.definitionCN: 副词，义为「也、此外」，用来补充另一点。

entries.definition: A formal connective introducing a further and stronger point.
entries.definitionCN: 正式连接词，引出进一步且更有力的论点。

entries.definition: An adverb marking what happens next in time.
entries.definitionCN: 副词，标示时间上接下来发生的事。

normalIntro.en: These hooks work with the shortest possible word: a sound, a rhyme and the physical act of joining.
normalIntro.cn: 下面几个钩子围绕这个最短的词展开：一个读音、一个韵脚和「连接」的实体动作。

normal.en: Say it weak in the middle of a sentence, 'bread'n milk', and strong when you list: 'bread AND milk'.
normal.cn: 在句中读弱，「面包嗯牛奶」；列举时读强，「面包 AND 牛奶」。

normal.en: It rhymes with band, hand, land and sand, so the short sound is easy to keep.
normal.cn: 它与 band、hand、land、sand 押韵，短音很容易记住。

normal.en: Picture a knot tied between two bundles, holding them as one load.
normal.cn: 想象两捆东西之间打了一个结，把它们变成一担。

normal.en: The word never changes shape: no -s, no -ed, no -ing, just and.
normal.cn: 这个词从不改变形态：不加 -s、-ed、-ing，就是 and。

normal.en: Two ands in one sentence usually mean a list is being built, not a new idea.
normal.cn: 一句话里出现两个 and，通常是在搭清单，而不是提出新观点。

abstract.en: And is the smallest promise that two things belong in the same sentence.
abstract.cn: and 是「两样东西属于同一句话」的最小承诺。

abstract.en: The word creates no meaning of its own; it only decides what stands together.
abstract.cn: 这个词本身不制造意义，只决定哪些东西站在一起。

abstract.en: Every list is a small act of trust that the items will not fight.
abstract.cn: 每一份清单都是一次小小的信任：这些条目不会互相打架。

examples.en: We sat by the fire and talked until midnight.
examples.cn: 我们坐在炉边，一直聊到午夜。

examples.en: The room was small and quiet.
examples.cn: 房间又小又安静。

examples.en: Add a little salt and the soup will taste better.
examples.cn: 加一点盐，汤的味道就会更好。

dict_mnemonic.text: 谐音「按的」：把两样东西按在一起，就是「和、与」。

root: 古英语 and、ond，源自原始日耳曼语 anda，与德语 und、荷兰语 en 同源。

sensesIntro.en: One joining act produces listing, sequence, conditional result and arithmetic addition.
sensesIntro.cn: 一个「连接」动作，生出了列举、顺承、条件结果与算术相加。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a fine cord tied between two objects, keeping them side by side.
core.cn: 核心意象：两件东西之间系着一根细绳，让它们并排在一起。

branches.en: THE LIST: the first sense keeps two items of the same kind together.
branches.cn: 清单线：第一个义项把两个同类条目放在一起。

branches.en: THE ORDER: the second sense reads the joined items as a sequence in time.
branches.cn: 顺序线：第二个义项把相连的条目读成时间上的先后。

branches.en: THE CONDITION: the third sense makes the first half a condition for the second.
branches.cn: 条件线：第三个义项让前半成为后半的条件。

branches.en: THE SUM: the fourth sense joins quantities by addition.
branches.cn: 和线：第四个义项用加法把数量连起来。

branches.en: THE THREAD: every sense is the same cord, only the things tied change.
branches.cn: 贯穿线：每个义项都是同一根绳，只是被系住的东西不同。

intro.en: And rarely takes affixes itself, but it is fixed inside many English compounds and phrases.
intro.cn: and 本身很少接词缀，但它被固定在许多英语复合词与短语里。

latinIntro.en: The word is Germanic rather than Latin, yet it appears inside compounds borrowed or built in English.
latinIntro.cn: 这个词属日耳曼语而非拉丁语，却出现在英语借用或自造的复合词中。

items.meaning: either both or one of the two
items.example: Bring a pen and/or a pencil.
items.exampleCN: 带一支钢笔和（或）一支铅笔。

items.meaning: a loud popular music style with strong rhythm
items.meaningCN: 一种节奏强烈的响亮流行音乐
items.example: The bar played rock and roll all night.
items.exampleCN: 酒吧整夜放着摇滚乐。

items.meaning: shown without colour, or divided into clear opposites
items.meaningCN: 无彩色的，或分成截然对立的两面
items.example: The old photograph is black and white.
items.exampleCN: 这张老照片是黑白的。

items.meaning: becoming successful and likely to do well
items.example: She is an up and coming young designer.
items.exampleCN: 她是一位崭露头角的年轻设计师。

items.example: We still meet now and then.
items.exampleCN: 我们仍时不时见面。

items.example: The shop sells bread, milk, eggs and so on.
items.exampleCN: 这家店卖面包、牛奶、鸡蛋等等。

items.example: They arrived safe and sound.
items.exampleCN: 他们安然抵达。

items.example: By and large, the plan worked.
items.exampleCN: 总的来说，这个计划奏效了。

definition_zh: 轶事；趣闻；秘闻；插叙的小故事
definition_en: a short, often amusing story about a real person or event, told to illustrate a point
core_image: 茶桌旁一个人压低声音，讲起一件亲历的小事，听的人都笑了
scene: 老茶馆里，几位老人围着方桌，其中一位拍着桌沿要讲往事。He told a funny anecdote about his first day at work.
sceneCN: 这里 anecdote 是「轶事、趣闻」（第 1 个义项：关于真人真事的短小故事）；句意为讲了一件关于他上班第一天的趣事。画面里有茶壶、方桌与围坐的老人。

pos.zh: 名词：轶事；趣闻；秘闻；插叙故事

derivatives.zh: 由本词加 -al 构成，义为「轶事的；传闻式的」
anecdotal 加 -ly 构成，义为「据轶闻所说；以传闻方式」
由本词加 -ist 构成，义为「爱讲轶事的人」

senses.title: A short amusing story about real people
senses.titleCN: 轶事：关于真人真事的短故事
senses.definition: a short story about a real incident or person, usually amusing and told to make a point
senses.definitionCN: 关于真实事件或人物的短故事，通常有趣，用来说明某个观点
senses.example: He opened the lecture with an anecdote about his grandfather.
senses.exampleCN: 他以一则关于祖父的轶事开场。
senses.why: Greek anekdota meant 'things not published'; the word still carries the flavour of something told rather than printed.
senses.whyCN: 希腊语 anekdota 意为「未发表的东西」，这个词至今仍带着「口耳相传而非刊印」的味道。

senses.title: A piece of unpublished gossip
senses.titleCN: 秘闻：未公开的内幕细节
senses.definition: a small, often private detail about a public person or event that is repeated informally
senses.definitionCN: 关于公众人物或事件、常在私下流传的细小私密细节
senses.example: The biography is full of anecdotes about the minister's temper.
senses.exampleCN: 这本传记满是关于那位部长脾气的秘闻。
senses.why: The original Greek title described secret history; the modern sense keeps that whiff of the not-quite-official.
senses.whyCN: 希腊语原题指「秘史」，现代义仍保留那一点「不太官方」的气息。

senses.title: A digression inside a longer work
senses.titleCN: 插叙：长篇作品中的小故事
senses.definition: a short digression or illustrative story inserted into a speech, essay or longer narrative
senses.definitionCN: 插入演讲、文章或较长叙事中的简短插叙或说明性故事
senses.example: The essay uses an anecdote to break up a long argument.
senses.exampleCN: 这篇文章用一则小故事打断冗长的论证。
senses.why: In writing, the anecdote works as a pause: a small real scene dropped into the middle of abstract argument.
senses.whyCN: 在写作中，轶事起到停顿作用：把一个真实的小场景放进抽象论证的中间。

intro.en: Anecdote began as the title of a secret history and became the name of any small telling story.
intro.cn: anecdote 起初是一部秘史的书名，后来变成任何短小讲述故事的名称。

items.en: Anekdota meant 'things not published', from an- 'not' and ekdidonai 'to publish out'.
items.cn: anekdota 意为「未发表的东西」，由 an-「不」与 ekdidonai「发表出去」构成。

items.en: The historian Procopius gave the title Anekdota to his secret account of the emperor Justinian's court.
items.cn: 史家普罗科匹厄斯把自己关于查士丁尼宫廷的秘史题为 Anekdota。

items.en: French turned the title into a common noun for a short unpublished detail, and English borrowed it.
items.cn: 法语把这个书名转为普通名词，指未公开的细小细节，英语再借入。

items.en: English anecdote first meant a secret detail of history; the modern 'short amusing story' sense grew later.
items.cn: 英语 anecdote 最初指历史的隐秘细节；现代「有趣的短故事」义是后来长出来的。

items.en: By the eighteenth century the word had softened from secret history into the everyday telling of a small incident.
items.cn: 到十八世纪，这个词已从秘史软化为日常讲述的一件小事。

items.en: Today an anecdote is welcome in speeches and essays, valued for being concrete rather than statistical.
items.cn: 如今轶事在演讲与文章中受欢迎，价值在于具体，而不在统计。

note.en: The look-alike group is the anecdote family; the near-meaning group holds kinds of short narrative.
note.cn: 形近组是 anecdote 词族；近义组收各类短小叙事。

entries.definition: Based on personal stories rather than systematic evidence.
entries.definitionCN: 基于个人讲述而非系统证据的。

entries.definition: In the manner of an anecdote, or according to stories rather than data.
entries.definitionCN: 以轶事的方式，或依据传闻而非数据。

entries.definition: A person fond of telling anecdotes.
entries.definitionCN: 爱讲轶事的人。

entries.definition: The general word for a told account of events, true or invented.
entries.definitionCN: 叙述事件的通用词，无论真实或虚构。

entries.definition: A story, often one that is old, invented or slightly exaggerated.
entries.definitionCN: 故事，常指古老的、虚构的或略有夸张的。

entries.definition: A factual report of what happened.
entries.definitionCN: 对所发生之事的纪实性叙述。

entries.definition: A short piece of writing or drama, lighter than a full story.
entries.definitionCN: 短小的文章或戏剧片段，比完整故事轻。

normalIntro.en: These hooks connect the word to its Greek secret title, its sound, and the picture of a table of listeners.
normalIntro.cn: 下面几个钩子把这个词与希腊语「秘史」书名、读音以及一桌听众的画面连起来。

normal.en: The an- at the front means not, and the rest once meant published: an anecdote began as an unpublished thing.
normal.cn: 开头的 an- 表示「不」，其余部分曾表示「发表」：anecdote 起初是「未发表的东西」。

normal.en: Say 'AN-ik-dote': three beats, like a short story told in three breaths.
normal.cn: 读作「AN-尼克-兜特」，三拍，像用三口讲完的小故事。

normal.en: Picture a circle of chairs and one person leaning forward to begin.
normal.cn: 想象一圈椅子，一个人俯身向前开始讲。

normal.en: Anecdote and antidote differ by one letter: one cures boredom, the other cures poison.
normal.cn: anecdote 与 antidote 只差一个字母：一个治无聊，一个解毒。

normal.en: The adjective anecdotal is the warning label: stories are not data.
normal.cn: 形容词 anecdotal 是警告标签：故事不等于数据。

abstract.en: An anecdote is a small door through which a large idea can enter a room.
abstract.cn: 轶事是一扇小门，宏大的想法可以由此进入一间屋子。

abstract.en: The word reminds us that unpublished things are often the most alive.
abstract.cn: 这个词提醒我们：未发表的东西往往最有生命力。

abstract.en: Every anecdote is a claim that one small scene can stand for a wider truth.
abstract.cn: 每一则轶事都在声称：一个小场景可以代表更广的真相。

examples.en: The teacher told an anecdote about a student who became a pilot.
examples.cn: 老师讲了一则关于一名学生后来成为飞行员的故事。

examples.en: His speech was full of anecdotes but short on evidence.
examples.cn: 他的演讲满是轶事，却缺少证据。

examples.en: She kept a notebook of anecdotes for future lectures.
examples.cn: 她记了一本轶事笔记，留着以后讲课用。

dict_mnemonic.text: 谐音「安尼克抖特」：安尼克抖着腿讲了一段小趣闻，逗得大家笑。

root: 希腊语 an-（不）+ ekdidonai（发表），anekdota 即「未发表的东西」，原为一部秘史的书名。

sensesIntro.en: The word moves from secret history to any short telling story, then to private gossip and to the digression inside a longer work.
sensesIntro.cn: 这个词从秘史走到任何短小讲述的故事，再到私下流传的秘闻，以及长篇中的插叙。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a small real incident pulled out of the flow of time and told across a table.
core.cn: 核心意象：从时间长河里抽出一件真实小事，在桌边讲给人听。

branches.en: THE TABLE: the first sense is the everyday telling of a small true story.
branches.cn: 茶桌线：第一个义项是日常讲述一件真实小事的本事。

branches.en: THE SECRET: the second sense keeps the original flavour of the unpublished detail.
branches.cn: 秘闻线：第二个义项保留「未公开细节」的原味。

branches.en: THE PAGE: the third sense places the small story inside a larger argument.
branches.cn: 书页线：第三个义项把小故事放进更大的论证里。

branches.en: THE ILLUSTRATION: both spoken and written anecdotes exist to make a point concrete.
branches.cn: 说明线：口讲与书写的轶事都是为了让观点变具体。

branches.en: THE DIGRESSION: gossip and inserted stories both interrupt the main line on purpose.
branches.cn: 插曲线：秘闻与插叙都故意打断主线。

intro.en: English builds the family with -al, -ally and -ist, and the stem remains anecdotal- before most suffixes.
intro.cn: 英语用 -al、-ally、-ist 扩展这个词族，多数后缀前的词干为 anecdotal-。

latinIntro.en: The Greek stem anekdot- reached English through French; the suffixes are English additions.
latinIntro.cn: 希腊词干 anekdot- 经法语进入英语，后缀都是英语后来添加的。

items.meaning: based on personal stories rather than proof
items.meaningCN: 基于个人讲述而非证据的
items.example: The evidence is only anecdotal.
items.exampleCN: 证据只是轶闻性质的。

items.meaning: by way of stories or reports
items.example: Anecdotally, the remedy seems to help.
items.exampleCN: 据传闻，这个疗法似乎有帮助。

items.example: The old captain was a born anecdotist.
items.exampleCN: 这位老船长天生爱讲轶事。

items.meaning: evidence made of stories, not measurements
items.meaningCN: 由故事而非测量构成的证据
items.example: Anecdotal evidence is easy to collect and hard to trust.
items.exampleCN: 轶闻证据容易收集，却难以信任。

items.meaning: a short story from one's own life
items.meaningCN: 来自本人生活的小故事
items.example: He opened with a personal anecdote.
items.exampleCN: 他以一则个人轶事开场。

items.meaning: a story repeated within a family
items.meaningCN: 家族内部反复讲述的故事
items.example: That family anecdote gets longer every year.
items.exampleCN: 那则家族轶事每年都变得更长。

items.meaning: a gathered set of short stories
items.example: The volume is an anecdote collection rather than a history.
items.exampleCN: 这卷书是轶事集，而不是史书。

items.meaning: history told through small personal stories
items.meaningCN: 通过个人小故事讲述的历史
items.example: The book offers an anecdotal history of the street.
items.exampleCN: 这本书提供了一条街的轶事史。

definition_zh: 愤怒；怒气；怒容；使发怒
definition_en: a strong feeling of being unfair treatment or harm, or to make someone feel that way
core_image: 胸口升起的一团热，压住声音，却让下颌绷紧
scene: 厨房里碗碟碰得叮当响，男人攥紧拳头，又慢慢松开。Her anger faded as soon as she saw the child's face.
sceneCN: 这里 anger 是「愤怒」（第 1 个义项：因不公或伤害而生的强烈情绪）；句意为一看到孩子的脸，她的怒气就消散了。画面里有厨房、碗碟与紧握的手。

pos.zh: 名词：愤怒；怒气；怒容
动词：使发怒；激怒

derivatives.zh: 由本词加 -y 构成，义为「生气的；愤怒的」
angry 加 -ly 构成，义为「愤怒地」
由本词加 -less 构成，义为「无怒气的；不生气的」

senses.title: The feeling of being wronged or harmed
senses.titleCN: 愤怒：因不公或伤害而生的情绪
senses.definition: a strong feeling caused by unfair treatment, injury or opposition
senses.definitionCN: 因不公平对待、伤害或对抗而产生的强烈情绪
senses.example: His voice shook with anger as he described the accident.
senses.exampleCN: 他描述那场事故时，声音因愤怒而发抖。
senses.why: Old Norse angr first meant grief and trouble; anger is the hot shape that trouble takes when it has an object to blame.
senses.whyCN: 古北欧语 angr 最初意为悲痛与烦扰；anger 就是烦扰找到可责怪的对象后所呈现的炽热形态。

senses.title: The outward sign of anger
senses.titleCN: 怒容：怒气的外在表现
senses.definition: the visible display of anger in a face, voice or manner
senses.definitionCN: 在面容、声音或举止上显露出来的怒气
senses.example: There was real anger in her eyes.
senses.exampleCN: 她眼里有真正的怒气。
senses.why: The feeling is invisible, so the word also names its traces: the tightened jaw, the raised voice.
senses.whyCN: 情绪本身看不见，于是这个词也用来指它的痕迹：绷紧的下颌、抬高的声音。

senses.title: To make someone angry
senses.titleCN: 使发怒；激怒
senses.definition: to cause someone to feel anger
senses.definitionCN: 使某人产生愤怒
senses.example: The delay angered passengers who had already waited hours.
senses.exampleCN: 延误激怒了已经等了几个小时的乘客。
senses.why: The noun becomes a verb: a person is made to hold the hot thing the noun names.
senses.whyCN: 名词变成动词：一个人被弄成盛着名词所指那团热东西的状态。

intro.en: Anger came from Old Norse, and it began as a word for trouble and grief rather than for rage.
intro.cn: anger 来自古北欧语，最初指烦扰与悲痛，而不是暴怒。

items.en: Angr meant 'grief, sorrow, trouble'. The word entered English through the Norse settlements.
items.cn: angr 意为「悲痛、忧伤、烦扰」，这个词经北欧人定居点进入英语。

items.en: The verb angra meant 'to grieve, distress', and it stands behind the later English verb.
items.cn: 动词 angra 意为「使悲痛、使苦恼」，是后来英语动词的来源。

items.en: The Norse words are related to Latin angere, 'to choke, distress', which also gave anguish and anxiety.
items.cn: 这些北欧词与拉丁语 angere「使窒息、使苦恼」相关，后者还生出 anguish 与 anxiety。

items.en: Middle English anger still meant affliction or trouble; the modern sense of wrath developed later.
items.cn: 中古英语 anger 仍指苦恼或烦扰；现代「愤怒」义是后来发展出来的。

items.en: By the sixteenth and seventeenth centuries the word had settled on the hot reaction to injury or insult.
items.cn: 到十六、十七世纪，这个词固定为对伤害或侮辱的炽热反应。

items.en: Psychology now treats anger as a normal signal, while everyday use still ranges from mild irritation to rage.
items.cn: 心理学如今把愤怒视为一种正常信号，而日常用法仍从轻微不快延伸到暴怒。

note.en: The look-alike group is the anger family; the near-meaning group holds stronger and weaker words for the same heat.
note.cn: 形近组是 anger 词族；近义组收同一团热气的强弱不同说法。

entries.definition: The adjective meaning feeling or showing anger.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，义为「感到或表现出愤怒的」。

entries.definition: The adverb meaning in an angry manner.
entries.definitionCN: 副词，义为「愤怒地」。

entries.definition: A rare adjective meaning without anger.
entries.definitionCN: 罕用形容词，义为「不生气的、无怒气的」。

entries.definition: Very strong anger that is hard to control.
entries.definitionCN: 难以控制的极强愤怒。

entries.definition: Wild, violent anger, often shown in action.
entries.definitionCN: 猛烈狂暴的愤怒，常表现为行动。

entries.definition: Mild annoyance at something small or repeated.
entries.definitionCN: 因小事或反复发生的事而产生的轻微恼怒。

entries.definition: A literary or formal word for great anger, often with a sense of punishment.
entries.definitionCN: 文学或正式用语，指盛怒，常带惩罚意味。

normalIntro.en: These hooks tie the word to its Norse origin, to its family of forms, and to the physical heat of the feeling.
normalIntro.cn: 下面几个钩子把这个词与北欧语来源、词族形式以及情绪的实体热度连起来。

normal.en: Anger first meant trouble, so think of a trouble that has caught fire.
normal.cn: anger 最初指烦扰，所以想象一团着了火的麻烦。

normal.en: The g is soft: 'ANG-ger', with the back of the tongue lifting like a held breath.
normal.cn: g 音较软，读「ANG-格尔」，舌根抬起，像憋住一口气。

normal.en: One letter turns the noun into the adjective: anger, angry.
normal.cn: 一个字母之差把名词变成形容词：anger、angry。

normal.en: Picture steam rising from a pot with the lid still on.
normal.cn: 想象锅盖还扣着，蒸汽却从边缘冒出来。

normal.en: In anger means while the heat is still in the body, not after it cools.
normal.cn: in anger 指热气还在体内的时候，而不是冷却之后。

abstract.en: Anger is grief that has found someone to blame.
abstract.cn: 愤怒是找到了责怪对象的悲痛。

abstract.en: The word is a warning light rather than an instruction.
abstract.cn: 这个词是警示灯，而不是行动指令。

abstract.en: Anger kept too long turns into something colder and harder to name.
abstract.cn: 怒气憋得太久，会变成更冷、更难命名的东西。

examples.en: She could not hide her anger at the unfair decision.
examples.cn: 她无法掩饰对这项不公决定的愤怒。

examples.en: He spoke in anger and regretted it later.
examples.cn: 他在气头上说了话，事后又后悔。

examples.en: The careless remark angered everyone in the room.
examples.cn: 那句轻率的话激怒了屋里的每个人。

dict_mnemonic.text: 谐音「昂哥」：昂着头、梗着脖子的大哥，一看就是气坏了。

root: 古北欧语 angr（悲痛、烦扰）与 angra（使苦恼），与拉丁语 angere（使窒息、使苦恼）同源。

sensesIntro.en: A Norse word for trouble becomes the name of the feeling, then of its visible signs, and finally of the act of causing it.
sensesIntro.cn: 一个指「烦扰」的北欧词，先成为情绪的名称，再指情绪的外显，最后指使人产生这种情绪的动作。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: heat rising in the chest, held behind a tightened jaw.
core.cn: 核心意象：胸口升起热气，被绷紧的下颌挡在后面。

branches.en: THE FEELING: the first sense is the inner heat itself.
branches.cn: 情绪线：第一个义项就是内在的那团热。

branches.en: THE FACE: the second sense is the heat showing on the outside.
branches.cn: 面容线：第二个义项是热气显露在外。

branches.en: THE CAUSE: the third sense is the act of putting that heat into someone else.
branches.cn: 致怒线：第三个义项是把这团热放进别人体内的动作。

branches.en: THE SIGNAL: feeling and display are the same message, one inside and one outside.
branches.cn: 信号线：情绪与表现是同一条信息，一内一外。

branches.en: THE CIRCUIT: anger can pass from person to person, which is why the verb exists.
branches.cn: 回路线：怒气能在人与人之间传递，动词义正因此存在。

intro.en: The family is small: -y makes the adjective, -ly the adverb, and -less the rare absence.
intro.cn: 这个词族不大：-y 构成形容词，-ly 构成副词，-less 表示罕见的「没有」。

latinIntro.en: The Norse stem anger- takes English suffixes; the related Latin angere appears in anguish and anxiety.
latinIntro.cn: 北欧词干 anger- 接英语后缀；相关的拉丁语 angere 则见于 anguish 与 anxiety。

items.example: He was angry with himself for forgetting.
items.exampleCN: 他因自己忘记而生气。

items.example: She closed the door angrily.
items.exampleCN: 她气冲冲地关上门。

items.example: His angerless reply surprised everyone.
items.exampleCN: 他毫无怒气的回答让所有人吃惊。

items.example: The angered crowd refused to leave.
items.exampleCN: 被激怒的人群拒绝离开。

items.example: It was an angering waste of time.
items.exampleCN: 那是令人愤怒的时间浪费。

items.meaning: a sudden short burst of anger
items.example: He threw the papers down in a fit of anger.
items.exampleCN: 他一怒之下把文件摔下。

items.example: The court ordered an anger management course.
items.exampleCN: 法院判他参加怒气管理课程。

items.meaning: anger felt at something clearly unjust
items.meaningCN: 因明显不公而生的义愤
items.example: Their righteous anger was hard to argue with.
items.exampleCN: 他们的义愤让人难以反驳。

definition_zh: 角；角度；视角；拐角；钓鱼；斜向移动；带倾向地报道
definition_en: the space between two lines or surfaces that meet, or a particular way of looking at something
core_image: 两条线在一个点相遇，张开一个口子，口子的大小决定了看法
scene: 木匠把木板斜靠在墙边，拿出量角器对准接缝。The carpenter checked the angle before cutting the wood.
sceneCN: 这里 angle 是「角、角度」（第 1 个义项：两条线相交形成的夹角）；句意为木匠在锯木头前先核对角度。画面里有木板、量角器与锯子。

pos.zh: 名词：角；角度；视角；拐角
动词：斜向移动；钓鱼；带倾向地报道

derivatives.zh: 由本词加 -ular 构成，义为「有角的；尖锐的；瘦削的」
angular 加 -ity 构成，义为「有角性；棱角分明」
angular 加 -ly 构成，义为「成角地；以棱角方式」
由本词加 -ed 构成，义为「成角度的；斜的」

senses.title: The space between two meeting lines
senses.titleCN: 角：两条线相交形成的夹角
senses.definition: the figure or space formed where two lines or surfaces meet, measured in degrees
senses.definitionCN: 两条线或两个面相遇处形成的图形或空间，以度数计量
senses.example: The two walls meet at a sharp angle.
senses.exampleCN: 两面墙以一个锐角相接。
senses.why: Latin angulus meant 'corner'; the geometric angle is the corner seen as a measurable opening.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁语 angulus 意为「角、拐角」，几何上的角就是把拐角看成一个可测量的开口。

senses.title: A point of view
senses.titleCN: 视角：看待事物的立场
senses.definition: a particular way of considering a situation, often chosen to make something look different
senses.definitionCN: 考虑某一情况的特定方式，常被选择以使事物呈现不同面貌
senses.example: Try looking at the problem from the customer's angle.
senses.exampleCN: 试着从顾客的角度来看这个问题。
senses.why: Where you stand changes what you see, so the geometric opening becomes a mental position.
senses.whyCN: 站的位置改变所见，于是几何上的开口变成了头脑中的立场。

senses.title: A corner of a room or street
senses.titleCN: 拐角：房间或街道的角落
senses.definition: a corner formed by two walls or edges, especially one where two surfaces meet
senses.definitionCN: 由两面墙或两条边形成的角落，尤指两个表面相接处
senses.example: The chair sat in the angle between the bookcase and the door.
senses.exampleCN: 椅子放在书柜与门之间的拐角处。
senses.why: This is the oldest physical sense: the actual corner where two surfaces turn into each other.
senses.whyCN: 这是最古老的实体义：两个表面彼此转折的那个实际角落。

senses.title: A sloping direction
senses.titleCN: 斜角：倾斜的方向或姿态
senses.definition: a position in which something is not straight up or flat but leans or slopes
senses.definitionCN: 某物不竖直也不水平、而是倾斜或斜靠的位置
senses.example: The picture hangs at a slight angle to the left.
senses.exampleCN: 那幅画略微向左倾斜地挂着。
senses.why: A sloping line is simply a line that meets the horizontal at an angle instead of lying on it.
senses.whyCN: 斜线不过是以某个角与水平线相交、而不是躺在水平线上的线。

senses.title: To fish with a hook
senses.titleCN: 钓鱼：用钩子捕鱼
senses.definition: to fish with a rod and hook, especially for a particular kind of fish
senses.definitionCN: 用钓竿和钩子捕鱼，尤指捕某种特定的鱼
senses.example: They angled for trout in the cold river.
senses.exampleCN: 他们在冰冷的河里钓鳟鱼。
senses.why: The fishing sense comes from a different Old English word for a hook, which happened to share the modern spelling.
senses.whyCN: 钓鱼义来自另一个古英语的「钩子」词，只是碰巧与现代拼写相同。

senses.title: To slant news toward a view
senses.titleCN: 带倾向地报道：让叙述偏向某一方
senses.definition: to present information so that it favours a particular interpretation or audience
senses.definitionCN: 呈现信息时使其偏向某种解释或某类受众
senses.example: The report was angled toward readers who already agreed.
senses.exampleCN: 这篇报道偏向那些本就认同的读者。
senses.why: The camera and the pen both choose an angle, and the chosen angle decides what the reader sees first.
senses.whyCN: 镜头与笔都在选角度，而被选中的角度决定了读者先看到什么。

intro.en: Angle has two sources that look alike today: the Latin word for a corner and an Old English word for a fish hook.
intro.cn: angle 有两个今天看来相似的来源：拉丁语表示「角」的词，以及古英语表示「鱼钩」的词。

items.en: Angulus meant 'corner, angle', and it also produced English angular and triangle.
items.cn: angulus 意为「角、拐角」，也生出英语的 angular 与 triangle。

items.en: Old French angle carried the geometric and spatial senses into Middle English.
items.cn: 古法语 angle 把几何与空间义带入中古英语。

items.en: A separate Old English word, angel, meant 'fish hook'; its verb form anglen meant to fish with one.
items.cn: 另一个古英语词 angel 意为「鱼钩」，其动词形式 anglen 指用钩钓鱼。

items.en: The two words converged in spelling, so one modern form now carries both the corner and the hook.
items.cn: 两个词在拼写上汇合，于是同一个现代词形同时承载「角」与「钩」。

items.en: Photography and journalism added the sense of a chosen viewpoint, extending the geometric image.
items.cn: 摄影与新闻业加上了「选定视角」的含义，延伸了几何意象。

note.en: The look-alike group is the angular family; the near-meaning group holds corners, viewpoints and slopes.
note.cn: 形近组是 angular 词族；近义组收拐角、视角与斜面类词。

entries.definition: Having angles, or bony and sharp in shape.
entries.definitionCN: 有角的，或形容瘦削、棱角分明的。

entries.definition: The quality of being angular.
entries.definitionCN: 有棱角、呈角状的性质。

entries.definition: A flat shape with three straight sides and three angles.
entries.definitionCN: 有三条直边和三个角的平面图形。

entries.definition: The point where two edges or walls meet.
entries.definitionCN: 两条边或两面墙相接的地方。

entries.definition: A person's way of thinking about a subject.
entries.definitionCN: 一个人对某个主题的思考方式。

entries.definition: A particular way of seeing things from one position.
entries.definitionCN: 从某一位置看事物的特定方式。

entries.definition: A slope or a bias in the way something is presented.
entries.definitionCN: 斜面，或呈现方式中的偏向。

normalIntro.en: These hooks link the word to the opening between two lines, to the camera, and to the fish hook that shares its spelling.
normalIntro.cn: 下面几个钩子把这个词与两线之间的开口、镜头，以及同形的鱼钩连起来。

normal.en: Picture a door half open: the gap between door and wall is the angle.
normal.cn: 想象一扇半开的门：门与墙之间的缺口就是角。

normal.en: Say 'ANG-gul': the hard g makes the word feel sharp, like a corner.
normal.cn: 读作「ANG-格尔」，硬 g 让这个词听起来有棱角。

normal.en: The same spelling also means to fish, because an old English hook had the same shape of word.
normal.cn: 同一拼写还表示钓鱼，因为古英语里表示钩子的词形恰好相同。

normal.en: Change the camera angle and the story changes, even if nothing in the room moves.
normal.cn: 改变机位角度，故事就变了，哪怕屋里什么都没动。

normal.en: A right angle is the square one; a sharp angle is the thin one.
normal.cn: right angle 是方方正正的直角，sharp angle 是尖细的锐角。

abstract.en: Every angle is a decision about what to leave outside the frame.
abstract.cn: 每个角度都是关于「把什么留在画框外」的决定。

abstract.en: Two people can stand in the same room and see different things, and both are telling the truth.
abstract.cn: 两个人站在同一间屋里却看到不同的东西，而两人都可能说的是真话。

abstract.en: The word reminds us that position is part of what we call knowledge.
abstract.cn: 这个词提醒我们：位置本身就是我们所称的「知识」的一部分。

examples.en: Measure the angle between the two lines.
examples.cn: 测量这两条线之间的夹角。

examples.en: Seen from this angle, the plan looks much cheaper.
examples.cn: 从这个角度看，这个方案显得便宜多了。

examples.en: He angled his chair toward the window.
examples.cn: 他把椅子斜转向窗户。

dict_mnemonic.text: 谐音「安格」：安格拿着量角器，一格一格量角度。

root: 拉丁语 angulus（角、拐角）；钓鱼义另出古英语 angel（鱼钩），两词在现代拼写中合流。

sensesIntro.en: The word runs from a measurable corner, to a chosen viewpoint, to the physical corner, a slope, a fish hook and a slanted report.
sensesIntro.cn: 这个词从可测量的角，走到选定的视角，再到实体拐角、斜面、鱼钩与带倾向的报道。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: two lines meet and open a gap, and the size of the gap decides what can be seen through it.
core.cn: 核心意象：两条线相遇张开一个口子，口子的大小决定能从中看见什么。

branches.en: THE GEOMETRY: the first sense is the measured opening itself.
branches.cn: 几何线：第一个义项就是被测量的开口本身。

branches.en: THE VIEW: the second sense turns the opening into a mental position.
branches.cn: 视角线：第二个义项把开口变成头脑中的立场。

branches.en: THE SPACE: the third and fourth senses keep the physical corner and the slope.
branches.cn: 空间线：第三、第四个义项保留实体拐角与斜面。

branches.en: THE HOOK: the fifth sense brings in the separate fishing word.
branches.cn: 鱼钩线：第五个义项引入另一个表示鱼钩的词。

branches.en: THE FRAME: the sixth sense shows a chosen angle controlling a report.
branches.cn: 取景线：第六个义项表明选定的角度如何支配报道。

intro.en: The Latin stem angul- builds adjectives and nouns of shape, and English compounds name tools and views.
intro.cn: 拉丁词干 angul- 构成形状类形容词与名词，英语复合词则命名工具与视角。

latinIntro.en: Latin angulus gave -angular and -angularity; Greek gonia supplies the -gon of polygon and the tri- of triangle.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 angulus 生出 -angular 与 -angularity；希腊语 gonia 提供 polygon 的 -gon 与 triangle 的 tri-。

items.example: The building has a stark angular facade.
items.exampleCN: 这座建筑有一面棱角分明的外墙。

items.example: The sculpture is admired for its angularity.
items.exampleCN: 这座雕塑因棱角分明而受赞赏。

items.example: The rooms are angularly arranged around a court.
items.exampleCN: 房间以棱角方式围绕庭院排列。

items.example: The mirror is angled toward the door.
items.exampleCN: 镜子斜对着门。

items.example: Draw a triangle with equal sides.
items.exampleCN: 画一个等边三角形。

items.example: The shelves meet the wall at a right angle.
items.exampleCN: 架子与墙成直角相接。

items.meaning: a bracket shaped like a sharp angle
items.example: Put the tag inside angle brackets.
items.exampleCN: 把标签放进尖括号里。

items.meaning: a lens that takes in a broad view
items.example: A wide-angle lens captured the whole square.
items.exampleCN: 广角镜头拍下了整个广场。

definition_zh: 生气的；愤怒的；愤怒的（言语或神情）；汹涌的；险恶的
definition_en: feeling or showing anger, or describing words, looks or natural forces that seem full of anger
core_image: 下颌绷紧、声音压低，像一锅盖不住的沸水
scene: 会议室里有人把文件摔在桌上，脸涨得通红。Her father was angry, but he said nothing.
sceneCN: 这里 angry 是「生气的」（第 1 个义项：感到愤怒的）；句意为她父亲很生气，却一句话也没说。画面里有会议室、文件与涨红的脸。

pos.zh: 形容词：生气的；愤怒的；汹涌的

derivatives.zh: 由本词加 -ly 构成，义为「愤怒地」
本词的名词形式，义为「愤怒；怒气」
由本词加 -ness 构成，义为「生气；怒气」（较少用）

senses.title: Feeling anger
senses.titleCN: 生气的：内心感到愤怒
senses.definition: feeling strong displeasure because of unfair treatment, injury or opposition
senses.definitionCN: 因不公平对待、伤害或对抗而感到强烈不满
senses.example: She was angry with him for breaking his promise.
senses.exampleCN: 她因为他违背承诺而对他生气。
senses.why: The adjective simply describes someone holding the heat that anger names.
senses.whyCN: 这个形容词只是描述一个人正盛着 anger 所指的那团热。

senses.title: Showing anger in words or looks
senses.titleCN: 愤怒的：言语或神情带怒气
senses.definition: describing words, looks or gestures that express anger
senses.definitionCN: 形容带有愤怒的言语、神情或动作
senses.example: He gave her an angry look across the table.
senses.exampleCN: 他隔着桌子狠狠看了她一眼。
senses.why: The feeling is lent to its signs: a look or a word can be called angry because it carries the same heat.
senses.whyCN: 情绪被借给了它的迹象：一道目光或一句话也可以叫 angry，因为它们带着同样的热。

senses.title: Threatening, as of weather or sea
senses.titleCN: 汹涌的：形容天气或海面险恶
senses.definition: describing a natural force that looks violent or threatening
senses.definitionCN: 形容看起来猛烈、带有威胁性的自然力量
senses.example: The angry sea broke against the harbour wall.
senses.exampleCN: 汹涌的海浪拍打着港湾的墙。
senses.why: Nature is imagined as a person in a rage: dark clouds and rough water become an angry face.
senses.whyCN: 自然被想象成一个暴怒的人：乌云与狂浪变成了一张愤怒的脸。

intro.en: Angry is the adjective built on anger, which came into English from Old Norse.
intro.cn: angry 是建立在 anger 之上的形容词，而 anger 来自古北欧语。

items.en: Angr meant 'grief, trouble', and its English descendant anger first meant affliction rather than rage.
