items.cn: angr 意为「悲痛、烦扰」，其英语后裔 anger 最初指苦恼而非暴怒。

items.en: The noun shifted toward the modern sense of wrath during the Middle English period.
items.cn: 在中古英语时期，这个名词逐渐转向现代的「愤怒」义。

items.en: English added the adjective suffix -y to the noun, giving angry, 'full of anger'.
items.cn: 英语给名词加上形容词后缀 -y，构成 angry，即「充满怒气的」。

items.en: The adjective is recorded from the fourteenth century onward and became common in the sixteenth.
items.cn: 这个形容词自十四世纪起有记录，到十六世纪变得常见。

items.en: The word widened from people to looks and words, and then to weather and sea.
items.cn: 这个词从人扩展到神情与言辞，再扩展到天气与海面。

note.en: The look-alike group is the anger family; the near-meaning group moves from mild annoyance to fury.
note.cn: 形近组是 anger 词族；近义组从轻微不快一路排到暴怒。

entries.definition: The noun for the feeling itself.
entries.definitionCN: 指这种情绪本身的名词。

entries.definition: The adverb describing how something is done in anger.
entries.definitionCN: 副词，描述带着怒气做某事的方式。

entries.definition: A rare noun for the state of being angry.
entries.definitionCN: 罕用名词，指「生气的状态」。

entries.definition: Mildly angry about something small or repeated.
entries.definitionCN: 因小事或反复发生的事而有点生气。

entries.definition: Extremely angry, almost out of control.
entries.definitionCN: 极其愤怒，几乎失控。

entries.definition: A British word for fairly angry or irritated.
entries.definitionCN: 英式说法，指相当生气或不快。

entries.definition: An informal word for angry, very common in American English.
entries.definitionCN: 口语中表示「生气」，在美式英语中很常见。

normalIntro.en: These hooks use the noun behind the adjective, the spelling change, and the picture of held-in heat.
normalIntro.cn: 下面几个钩子用到形容词背后的名词、拼写变化，以及「憋住的热」这一画面。

normal.en: Angry is anger plus y: full of anger, the way a cup is full of water.
normal.cn: angry 就是 anger 加 y：盛满怒气，就像杯子盛满水。

normal.en: The y turns to i before -ly: angry becomes angrily, not angryly.
normal.cn: 加 -ly 时 y 变 i：angry 变成 angrily，而不是 angryly。

normal.en: Say 'ANG-gree': the first beat is heavy, like a jaw tightening.
normal.cn: 读作「ANG-格瑞」，第一拍很重，像下颌绷紧。

normal.en: You are angry with a person but angry at a thing or an action.
normal.cn: angry with 接人，angry at 接事情或行为。

normal.en: An angry sea has no feelings; the word lends a human face to the weather.
normal.cn: 愤怒的海并没有情绪；这个词把一张人脸借给了天气。

abstract.en: Being angry is a fact; being angry at everyone is a choice.
abstract.cn: 生气是一个事实；对所有人都生气则是一种选择。

abstract.en: The word describes heat, not direction, and heat without direction is dangerous.
abstract.cn: 这个词描述的是热度，不是方向，而没有方向的热是危险的。

abstract.en: An angry silence often says more than an angry sentence.
abstract.cn: 愤怒的沉默常常比愤怒的句子说得更多。

examples.en: He gets angry when people interrupt him.
examples.cn: 别人打断他时，他会生气。

examples.en: She wrote an angry letter and then tore it up.
examples.cn: 她写了一封愤怒的信，然后把它撕了。

examples.en: The angry sky warned them to turn back.
examples.cn: 险恶的天空警告他们回头。

dict_mnemonic.text: 谐音「安格瑞」：安格瑞一皱眉，大家都知道他生气了。

root: 由 anger（古北欧语 angr「悲痛、烦扰」）加形容词后缀 -y 构成，义为「充满怒气的」。

sensesIntro.en: The adjective begins with a person's feeling, extends to the words and looks that carry it, and finally to a threatening sea or sky.
sensesIntro.cn: 这个形容词从人的感受出发，扩展到承载怒气的言辞与神情，最后到险恶的海与天。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a tightly closed jaw with heat pressing against it from inside.
core.cn: 核心意象：紧闭的下颌，里面的热气不断往上顶。

branches.en: THE FEELING: the first sense is the inner heat of a person.
branches.cn: 感受线：第一个义项是人的内在热气。

branches.en: THE SIGNS: the second sense is the heat showing in words and looks.
branches.cn: 迹象线：第二个义项是热气在言辞与神情中显现。

branches.en: THE WEATHER: the third sense lends the human face to sea and sky.
branches.cn: 天气线：第三个义项把人的面孔借给海与天。

branches.en: THE SAME HEAT: feeling and display are one state seen from inside and outside.
branches.cn: 同热线：感受与表现是同一状态的内外两面。

branches.en: THE SHARED SHAPE: sharp words and rough waves share the same imagined face.
branches.cn: 共形线：尖刻的话与狂暴的浪共享同一张想象的脸。

intro.en: The adjective takes -ly for the adverb and -ness for the rare noun, and English compounds extend it.
intro.cn: 这个形容词加 -ly 成副词、加 -ness 成罕用名词，英语复合词又进一步扩展。

latinIntro.en: The suffix -y here is Germanic, not Latin; the root belongs to the Norse and Germanic layer of English.
latinIntro.cn: 这里的 -y 属日耳曼语而非拉丁语；词根属于英语的北欧与日耳曼层次。

items.example: She slammed the book down angrily.
items.exampleCN: 她气冲冲地把书摔下。

items.example: His anger slowly cooled.
items.exampleCN: 他的怒气慢慢冷却。

items.example: A sudden angriness came over him.
items.exampleCN: 一阵怒气突然袭上他。

items.example: He grew angrier as the wait continued.
items.exampleCN: 等待越久，他越生气。

items.example: That was the angriest she had ever been.
items.exampleCN: 那是她最生气的一次。

items.example: Angry words were exchanged at the door.
items.exampleCN: 门口有人交换了愤怒的言辞。

items.example: The angry sea kept the boats in port.
items.exampleCN: 汹涌的海面让船只留在港内。

items.example: An angry silence filled the car.
items.exampleCN: 车里充满愤怒的沉默。

definition_zh: 动物；走兽；（贬）畜生；动物性的
definition_en: a living creature that can move and feel, as opposed to a plant, or the bodily part of human nature
core_image: 草地上抖掉雨水的毛茸茸身体，凭本能行动
scene: 雨后的草地上，一只小兽抖掉皮毛上的水珠。The animal shook the rain from its fur and ran off.
sceneCN: 这里 animal 是「动物」（第 1 个义项：会活动、有感觉的生物）；句意为那只动物抖掉毛上的雨水跑开了。画面里有草地、小兽与水珠。

pos.zh: 名词：动物；走兽；畜生（贬义）
形容词：动物的；肉体上的

derivatives.zh: 由本词加 -istic 构成，义为「兽性的；动物般的」
由本词加 -ity 构成，义为「动物性；兽性」
由本词加 -ism 构成，义为「动物性主张；兽性行为」（罕用）

senses.title: A living creature that is not a plant
senses.titleCN: 动物：非植物的活物
senses.definition: a living being that can move, feed and respond to its surroundings, as distinct from a plant
senses.definitionCN: 能移动、进食并对周围作出反应的生物，与植物相对
senses.example: The forest is home to hundreds of kinds of animals.
senses.exampleCN: 这片森林是数百种动物的家园。
senses.why: Latin animalis meant 'having breath'; an animal is literally a breathing thing, the opposite of a plant.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁语 animalis 意为「有气息的」，动物字面上就是会呼吸的东西，与植物相对。

senses.title: A beast rather than a bird or fish
senses.titleCN: 走兽：口语中与鸟、鱼相对的兽类
senses.definition: in everyday speech, a four-legged creature or a mammal, as opposed to a bird, fish or insect
senses.definitionCN: 日常口语中指四足动物或哺乳动物，与鸟、鱼、昆虫相对
senses.example: The children were excited to see the animals at the zoo.
senses.exampleCN: 孩子们在动物园看到那些走兽时很兴奋。
senses.why: Everyday use narrows the scientific category: the furry four-legged creature is the animal par excellence.
senses.whyCN: 日常用法把科学分类收窄：毛茸茸的四足动物才是典型的 animal。

senses.title: A brutal person, used as an insult
senses.titleCN: 畜生：贬称残暴或粗野的人
senses.definition: a person who behaves in a cruel, violent or uncivilized way
senses.definitionCN: 行为残暴、粗暴或缺乏教养的人
senses.example: Only an animal would treat a child like that.
senses.exampleCN: 只有畜生才会那样对待一个孩子。
senses.why: The word strips a person of reason: whoever behaves without human restraint is pushed back into the category of beasts.
senses.whyCN: 这个词剥夺了一个人的理性：谁行为不受人的约束，就被推回兽类。

senses.title: Belonging to the body rather than the mind
senses.titleCN: 动物性的：属于肉体而非精神
senses.definition: relating to the physical or instinctive part of human nature rather than its thinking part
senses.definitionCN: 与人性的肉体或本能部分相关，而非思考部分
senses.example: He was tired of fighting his animal urges.
senses.exampleCN: 他厌倦了与自己的动物本能对抗。
senses.why: The noun becomes an adjective for what humans share with beasts: appetite, instinct and the body itself.
senses.whyCN: 名词转作形容词，指人与兽共享的部分：食欲、本能以及身体本身。

intro.en: Animal is a Latin word built on anima, 'breath or soul', and it once described any living being, plants included.
intro.cn: animal 是建立在 anima「气息、灵魂」之上的拉丁词，最初可指任何活物，植物也算。

items.en: Anima meant 'breath, air, soul', the invisible thing that was thought to keep a body alive.
items.cn: anima 意为「气息、空气、灵魂」，被认为是维持身体存活的看不见之物。

items.en: Animalis was an adjective meaning 'having breath, living', used of anything alive.
items.cn: animalis 是形容词，意为「有气息的、活的」，可用于任何活物。

items.en: The neuter noun animal meant 'a living being'; in later use it narrowed to creatures that move.
items.cn: 中性名词 animal 意为「活物」；后世用法收窄到会活动的生物。

items.en: Old French animal brought the narrowed sense into English.
items.cn: 古法语 animal 把这个收窄后的词义带入英语。

items.en: English adopted the word in the fourteenth century, and the exact first record is uncertain.
items.cn: 英语在十四世纪采用这个词，确切的首条记录不确定。

items.en: Biology fixed the scientific sense, while everyday speech kept the narrower beast and the insulting human use.
items.cn: 生物学固定了科学义，而日常语言保留了较窄的「走兽」义与骂人的用法。

note.en: The look-alike group gathers words from the same anima root; the near-meaning group gathers living-creature words of different breadth.
note.cn: 形近组收同一 anima 词根的词；近义组收宽窄不同的「生物」类词。

entries.definition: To give life or movement to something, or alive.
entries.definitionCN: 赋予生命或活力，或指「有生命的」。

entries.definition: The technique of making drawings or models appear to move.
entries.definitionCN: 让图画或模型看起来会动的技术。

entries.definition: Not alive, without life or movement.
entries.definitionCN: 没有生命的，无生气的。

entries.definition: Any living being, often used with sympathy or wonder.
entries.definitionCN: 任何活物，常带怜惜或惊奇色彩。

entries.definition: A large or wild animal, or a brutal person.
entries.definitionCN: 大型或野生动物，也可指残暴的人。

entries.definition: A warm-blooded animal that feeds its young with milk.
entries.definitionCN: 以乳汁哺育幼崽的温血动物。

entries.definition: Animals and plants living freely in nature.
entries.definitionCN: 在自然中自由生活的动物与植物。

normalIntro.en: These hooks connect the word to breath, to the zoo, and to the difference between a creature and a person.
normalIntro.cn: 下面几个钩子把这个词与「气息」、动物园，以及「兽」与「人」的差别连起来。

normal.en: The root anima means breath, so an animal is a breathing thing.
normal.cn: 词根 anima 意为「气息」，所以 animal 就是会呼吸的东西。

normal.en: Say 'AN-i-mal': three light beats, like an animal moving in three steps.
normal.cn: 读作「AN-尼-莫」，三拍轻快，像动物走三步。

normal.en: The plural animals simply adds an s, unlike the irregular plurals of many beast names.
normal.cn: 复数 animals 只加 s，不像许多兽名的复数那样不规则。

normal.en: In science every insect is an animal; in the zoo the word often means the furry ones.
normal.cn: 科学上昆虫也是 animal；在动物园里，这个词常指毛茸茸的那些。

normal.en: Calling a person an animal is always an insult, never a compliment.
normal.cn: 把人称作 animal 永远是骂人，绝不是称赞。

abstract.en: The word draws a line between us and them, then quietly admits we are also breathing things.
abstract.cn: 这个词在我们与它们之间画了一条线，又悄悄承认我们也是会呼吸的东西。

abstract.en: To call someone an animal is to say that reason has failed.
abstract.cn: 把某人叫作动物，等于说理性已经失效。

abstract.en: Animals do not need the word; only the creature that invented it does.
abstract.cn: 动物不需要这个词，只有发明了它的生物才需要。

examples.en: The animal hid under the leaves until the rain stopped.
examples.cn: 那只动物躲在叶子下面，直到雨停。

examples.en: Every animal in the shelter needs food and clean water.
examples.cn: 收容所里的每只动物都需要食物和干净的水。

examples.en: Scientists study animal behaviour in the wild.
examples.cn: 科学家研究野外的动物行为。

dict_mnemonic.text: 谐音「安尼莫」：安尼莫养了一只小动物，取名叫莫莫。

root: 拉丁语 anima（气息、灵魂）+ -alis（形容词后缀），animal 原义「有气息的活物」。

sensesIntro.en: The word covers every living creature, narrows in everyday speech to beasts, becomes an insult for cruel people, and an adjective for the body.
sensesIntro.cn: 这个词覆盖所有活物，日常语言中收窄为走兽，又变成骂残暴之人的词，并作形容词指肉体。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a warm body that breathes, moves and acts on instinct.
core.cn: 核心意象：一具温热的身体，会呼吸、会移动、按本能行动。

branches.en: THE LIVING KIND: the first sense is any breathing creature.
branches.cn: 生物线：第一个义项是任何会呼吸的生物。

branches.en: THE BEAST: the second sense narrows the word to furry four-legged creatures.
branches.cn: 走兽线：第二个义项把词收窄到毛茸茸的四足动物。

branches.en: THE INSULT: the third sense pushes a cruel person back into the beast category.
branches.cn: 骂人线：第三个义项把残暴的人推回兽类。

branches.en: THE BODY: the fourth sense names what humans share with beasts.
branches.cn: 肉体线：第四个义项命名人与兽共享的部分。

branches.en: THE CATEGORY: the wide scientific sense and the narrow everyday sense sit inside one word.
branches.cn: 分类线：宽泛的科学义与狭窄的日常义装在同一个词里。

intro.en: The stem animal- takes -istic, -ity and -ism, and English compounds name domains and rights.
intro.cn: 词干 animal- 接 -istic、-ity、-ism，英语复合词则命名领域与权利。

latinIntro.en: Latin animal and animalis stand behind the family; animate and inanimate come from the same anima.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 animal 与 animalis 是这个词族的基础；animate 与 inanimate 同出 anima。

items.meaning: like a beast, driven by instinct
items.meaningCN: 像野兽的，受本能驱使的
items.example: The crowd turned animalistic in the heat.
items.exampleCN: 人群在酷热中变得像野兽。

items.meaning: the state of being an animal
items.example: The novel explores the animality beneath civility.
items.exampleCN: 这部小说探究文明之下的兽性。

items.meaning: belief or behaviour centred on animal nature
items.meaningCN: 以动物性为中心的主张或行为
items.example: The philosophy was criticized as animalism.
items.exampleCN: 这种哲学被批评为动物主义。

items.example: Cruelty can animalize a whole crowd.
items.exampleCN: 残忍能让整个人群变得像野兽。

items.meaning: a place that cares for homeless animals
items.example: She volunteers at the animal shelter.
items.exampleCN: 她在动物收容所做志愿者。

items.meaning: all animals considered as one group
items.meaningCN: 作为一个整体的全部动物
items.example: Insects make up most of the animal kingdom.
items.exampleCN: 昆虫构成动物界的大部分。

items.meaning: the claim that animals deserve protection
items.meaningCN: 主张动物应受保护的权利
items.example: The group campaigns for animal rights.
items.exampleCN: 这个组织为动物权利奔走。

items.meaning: the farming and care of animals
items.example: He studied animal husbandry at college.
items.exampleCN: 他在大学学习畜牧。

definition_zh: 脚踝；踝关节；踝部
definition_en: the joint between the foot and the lower leg, or the narrow part of the leg just above the foot
core_image: 脚与小腿之间那个细细的转弯处，走路时承担全部重量
scene: 雨后的石阶湿滑，女孩一脚踩空，蹲下去揉脚。She twisted her ankle on the wet stone steps.
sceneCN: 这里 ankle 是「脚踝」（第 1 个义项：脚与小腿相接的部位）；句意为她在湿滑的石阶上扭伤了脚踝。画面里有石阶、雨水与蹲下的女孩。

pos.zh: 名词：脚踝；踝关节；踝部

derivatives.zh: 由本词加 -let 构成，义为「脚链；踝饰」
由本词与 deep 复合，义为「深及脚踝的」
由本词与 length 复合，义为「长及脚踝的」

senses.title: The joint between foot and leg
senses.titleCN: 脚踝：脚与小腿相接的关节
senses.definition: the joint that connects the foot to the lower leg and allows the foot to bend
senses.definitionCN: 连接脚与小腿、使脚能够弯曲的关节
senses.example: He broke his ankle playing football.
senses.exampleCN: 他踢足球时摔断了脚踝。
senses.why: Old English named this bend in the leg; the joint is where the straight line of the leg turns into the foot.
senses.whyCN: 古英语命名了腿上的这个弯折处；这个关节正是腿的直线转为脚的地方。

senses.title: The narrow part above the foot
senses.titleCN: 踝部：脚上方那段细窄处
senses.definition: the narrow part of the leg just above the foot, considered as a body area rather than a joint
senses.definitionCN: 脚上方那段细窄的腿部，作为身体部位而非关节来看待
senses.example: The water came up to her ankles.
senses.exampleCN: 水没过了她的脚踝。
senses.why: The joint gives its name to the whole narrow region around it, a common habit in body words.
senses.whyCN: 关节的名字被借给了它周围的整段细窄区域，这是身体词汇常见的做法。

senses.title: The part of a garment covering this area
senses.titleCN: 踝部：衣物覆盖脚踝的部分
senses.definition: the part of a sock, shoe or trouser that covers or reaches the ankle
senses.definitionCN: 袜子、鞋子或裤子覆盖或到达脚踝的部分
senses.example: These ankle socks slip down when I walk.
senses.exampleCN: 这双短袜一走就往下滑。
senses.why: Clothing borrows the body's map: the part that sits at the ankle is simply called the ankle.
senses.whyCN: 衣物借用了身体的地图：位于脚踝处的部分就直接被称为 ankle。

intro.en: Ankle is an Old English body word, and its odd spelling reflects a long chain of sound changes.
intro.cn: ankle 是一个古英语的身体词，它古怪的拼写反映了一长串语音变化。

items.en: Ancleow named the ankle; related forms appear in Old Norse and other Germanic languages.
items.cn: ancleow 指脚踝；相关形式也见于古北欧语与其他日耳曼语言。

items.en: The Germanic word is reconstructed with a sense of something bent or hooked, describing the bend of the leg.
items.cn: 重构的日耳曼语词带有「弯曲、带钩」的意思，描述腿的弯折处。

items.en: The deeper root is associated with bending, and the same idea appears in other body words for joints.
items.cn: 更深的词根与「弯曲」相关，同一观念也出现在其他表示关节的身体词中。

items.en: Middle English reduced the old form to ankle, and the modern spelling was fixed early.
items.cn: 中古英语把古旧形式简化为 ankle，现代拼写很早就固定了。

items.en: The word now names the joint, the narrow region and the part of clothing that meets it.
items.cn: 这个词如今既指关节，也指细窄区域，以及与之相接的衣物部位。

note.en: The look-alike group is built with ankle in compounds; the near-meaning group names neighbouring parts of the leg and foot.
note.cn: 形近组由 ankle 构成的复合词组成；近义组命名腿脚相邻的部位。

entries.definition: A piece of jewellery worn around the ankle.
entries.definitionCN: 戴在脚踝上的饰物。

entries.definition: Deep enough to reach the ankles.
entries.definitionCN: 深到脚踝的。

entries.definition: Long enough to reach the ankles, said of clothes.
entries.definitionCN: 长及脚踝的，用于衣物。

entries.definition: The back part of the foot below the ankle.
entries.definitionCN: 脚踝下方脚的后部。

entries.definition: The part of the body at the end of the leg, used for standing.
entries.definitionCN: 腿末端用于站立的部分。

entries.definition: The fleshy back part of the lower leg.
entries.definitionCN: 小腿后部肌肉丰满的地方。

entries.definition: The front part of the lower leg.
entries.definitionCN: 小腿的前部。

normalIntro.en: These hooks use the bend in the leg, the spelling, and the everyday image of water at the ankle.
normalIntro.cn: 下面几个钩子用到腿上的弯折、拼写，以及「水没到脚踝」的日常画面。

normal.en: The word hides an old bend: the ankle is where the leg turns into the foot.
normal.cn: 这个词藏着一个古老的「弯折」：脚踝正是腿转为脚的地方。

normal.en: Say 'AN-kl': the k is swallowed quickly, like a foot landing.
normal.cn: 读作「AN-克欧」，k 音很快吞掉，像脚落地。

normal.en: The plural ankles is regular, so the spelling stays safe.
normal.cn: 复数 ankles 规则变化，拼写不会出岔子。

normal.en: An anklet is a little ankle: the -let suffix makes things small.
normal.cn: anklet 就是「小脚踝」：-let 后缀表示小。

normal.en: Water up to the ankle is the classic image of a shallow flood.
normal.cn: 水没到脚踝，是浅水漫溢的经典画面。

abstract.en: The ankle is the quiet hinge that makes walking possible.
abstract.cn: 脚踝是让走路成为可能的安静铰链。

abstract.en: Small joints carry large weights, which is why they fail first.
abstract.cn: 小关节承担大重量，所以它们最先出问题。

abstract.en: A twisted ankle teaches you how much you relied on something you never noticed.
abstract.cn: 扭伤的脚踝会让你明白，自己有多依赖一个从未留意的东西。

examples.en: She wore a thin silver chain around her ankle.
examples.cn: 她脚踝上戴着一条细银链。

examples.en: The cold water reached his ankles in seconds.
examples.cn: 冰冷的水几秒钟就漫到他的脚踝。

examples.en: The doctor wrapped the injured ankle tightly.
examples.cn: 医生把受伤的脚踝紧紧包扎起来。

dict_mnemonic.text: 谐音「安扣」：鞋带在脚踝那里安一个扣，走起来才稳。

root: 古英语 ancleow（脚踝），源自日耳曼语表示「弯曲」的词根，指腿与脚相接的弯折处。

sensesIntro.en: The word names the joint, then the narrow region around it, and finally the part of clothing that covers it.
sensesIntro.cn: 这个词先指关节，再指关节周围的细窄区域，最后指覆盖该处的衣物部分。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a narrow hinge where the straight leg bends into the flat foot.
core.cn: 核心意象：笔直的腿弯成平放的脚时，那个细窄的铰链处。

branches.en: THE JOINT: the first sense is the hinge itself.
branches.cn: 关节线：第一个义项就是那个铰链本身。

branches.en: THE REGION: the second sense is the narrow area around the hinge.
branches.cn: 区域线：第二个义项是铰链周围的细窄地带。

branches.en: THE CLOTH: the third sense is the garment part that sits there.
branches.cn: 衣物线：第三个义项是位于该处的衣物部分。

branches.en: THE BODY MAP: joint and region share one name because they share one place.
branches.cn: 身体地图线：关节与区域共用一个名字，因为它们在同一个位置。

branches.en: THE MEASURE: both water depth and sock length are measured at the ankle.
branches.cn: 量度线：水深与袜长都以脚踝为量度。

intro.en: English builds ankle compounds with -let, deep and length, and with clothing and injury words.
intro.cn: 英语用 -let、deep、length 以及衣物与损伤类词构成 ankle 的复合词。

latinIntro.en: The word is Germanic, not Latin; the -let suffix came into English through French.
latinIntro.cn: 这个词属日耳曼语而非拉丁语；-let 后缀是经法语进入英语的。

items.meaning: a small ornament worn at the ankle
items.example: She bought a silver anklet at the market.
items.exampleCN: 她在市场上买了一条银脚链。

items.meaning: deep enough to cover the ankles
items.example: The path was ankle-deep in mud.
items.exampleCN: 小路上的泥深到脚踝。

items.example: She wore an ankle-length coat.
items.exampleCN: 她穿了一件长及脚踝的外套。

items.meaning: a bone forming part of the ankle joint
items.example: He fractured a small ankle bone.
items.exampleCN: 他摔裂了一块小的踝骨。

items.meaning: the joint connecting foot and leg
items.example: The ankle joint allows the foot to flex.
items.exampleCN: 踝关节让脚能够屈伸。

items.meaning: socks that end at the ankle
items.example: He packed three pairs of ankle socks.
items.exampleCN: 他装了三双短袜。

items.meaning: an injury to the ligaments of the ankle
items.example: A bad ankle sprain kept her out for weeks.
items.exampleCN: 严重的踝扭伤让她缺席数周。

items.meaning: a strap that fastens around the ankle
items.example: The sandal has a thin ankle strap.
items.exampleCN: 这双凉鞋有一条细踝带。

definition_zh: 周年纪念日；周年纪念；周年
definition_en: a date on which an event is remembered each year, or the celebration held on that date
core_image: 日历上被红笔圈住的那一天，每年都会回来一次
scene: 老夫妻在餐桌前点起一支蜡烛，桌上摆着两张旧照片。They celebrated their fiftieth anniversary in the same small restaurant.
sceneCN: 这里 anniversary 是「周年纪念日」（第 1 个义项：每年回到的那个纪念日期）；句意为他们在同一家小餐馆庆祝了五十周年。画面里有蜡烛、旧照片与餐桌。

pos.zh: 名词：周年纪念日；周年纪念；周年

derivatives.zh: 由本词加 -ial 构成，义为「周年纪念的」（罕用）
由本词加 -ly 构成，义为「按周年方式地」（罕用）

senses.title: The yearly date of a past event
senses.titleCN: 周年纪念日：每年回到的那个日期
senses.definition: the date each year that matches the date of an important past event
senses.definitionCN: 每年与过去某件重要事件日期相同的那一天
senses.example: Their anniversary falls on the first day of spring.
senses.exampleCN: 他们的纪念日恰在春天的第一天。
senses.why: Latin anniversarius meant 'returning every year'; the word marks a date that comes back like a turning wheel.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁语 anniversarius 意为「每年返回的」，这个词标示一个像轮子转动般不断回来的日期。

senses.title: The celebration held on that date
senses.titleCN: 周年纪念：当天的庆祝活动
senses.definition: a celebration or ceremony held to mark such a date
senses.definitionCN: 为纪念这一日期而举行的庆祝或仪式
senses.example: The school held a large anniversary for its hundredth year.
senses.exampleCN: 学校为建校一百周年举行了盛大的纪念活动。
senses.why: The date and the party share one name because the party exists only to make the date visible.
senses.whyCN: 日期与庆祝共用一个名字，因为庆祝只是为了把那个日期变得看得见。

senses.title: A numbered year of continuing existence
senses.titleCN: 周年：第几个年头的计数
senses.definition: a particular numbered year since something began, as in a fifth or fiftieth anniversary
senses.definitionCN: 自某事物开始以来的特定第几年，如五周年或五十周年
senses.example: The company marked its tenth anniversary with a small party.
senses.exampleCN: 公司用一场小型聚会纪念成立十周年。
senses.why: Counting the returns turns the date into a number: the wheel has come round ten times.
senses.whyCN: 把一次次回转数下来，日期就变成了数字：轮子已经转了十圈。

intro.en: Anniversary joins the Latin words for year and turning, and it entered English through the medieval church.
intro.cn: anniversary 把拉丁语中表示「年」与「转动」的词连在一起，经中世纪教会进入英语。

items.en: Annus meant 'year', and it also gives English annual and annuity.
items.cn: annus 意为「年」，也生出英语的 annual 与 annuity。

items.en: Vertere meant 'to turn', the image behind the year coming round again.
items.cn: vertere 意为「转动」，正是「一年又转回来」这一意象的来源。

items.en: Anniversarius meant 'returning annually', built from annus and vertere.
items.cn: anniversarius 意为「每年返回的」，由 annus 与 vertere 构成。

items.en: The church used anniversarium for a mass said each year for a dead person.
items.cn: 教会用 anniversarium 指每年为亡者举行的弥撒。

items.en: English borrowed the word in the thirteenth century; the exact first record is uncertain.
items.cn: 英语在十三世纪借入这个词，确切的首条记录不确定。

items.en: The religious origin faded, and the word now covers weddings, companies, battles and births.
items.cn: 宗教来源逐渐淡去，这个词如今覆盖婚礼、公司、战役与诞辰。

note.en: The look-alike group shares the Latin root for year; the near-meaning group names other dates and celebrations.
note.cn: 形近组共享拉丁语「年」的词根；近义组收其他日期与庆典类词。

entries.definition: Happening once every year, or a plant that lives one year.
entries.definitionCN: 每年发生一次的，或指一年生植物。

entries.definition: Once a year, or every year.
entries.definitionCN: 每年一次地，或年年地。

entries.definition: A fixed sum paid each year, usually for life.
entries.definitionCN: 每年支付的固定金额，通常终身支付。

entries.definition: The yearly date on which a person was born.
entries.definitionCN: 一个人出生的那个每年回到的日期。

entries.definition: A special anniversary, often a fiftieth or twenty-fifth.
entries.definitionCN: 特殊的周年纪念，常指五十或二十五周年。

entries.definition: A ceremony or act of remembering an important person or event.
entries.definitionCN: 纪念重要人物或事件的仪式或行为。

entries.definition: An important point in a process or life, often marked by a date.
entries.definitionCN: 进程或人生中的重要节点，常以某个日期标记。

normalIntro.en: These hooks use the year-and-turning root, the long spelling, and the picture of a circled calendar date.
normalIntro.cn: 下面几个钩子用到「年与转动」的词根、较长的拼写，以及「日历上被圈住的一天」这一画面。

normal.en: Ann- means year and vers- means turn, so an anniversary is the year turning round again.
normal.cn: ann- 表示年，vers- 表示转，所以 anniversary 就是一年又转回来。

normal.en: Say it 'an-i-VER-sa-ry': the stress sits in the middle, like a date standing out in a calendar.
normal.cn: 读作「安尼-VER-色-瑞」，重音在中间，像日历上突出的那一天。

normal.en: The plural swaps y for ies: anniversaries, just like libraries and memories.
normal.cn: 复数把 y 变 ies：anniversaries，就像 libraries 与 memories。

normal.en: Picture a red circle around one square of a calendar, drawn again every year.
normal.cn: 想象日历上有一个格子被红笔圈住，每年都会重画一次。

normal.en: Wedding, wedding anniversary; company, company anniversary: the word always needs its owner.
normal.cn: 婚礼配结婚纪念日，公司配公司周年：这个词总要有个归属者。

abstract.en: An anniversary is time made countable and then made personal.
abstract.cn: 周年纪念是把时间变成可数的，再变成私人的。

abstract.en: The date returns whether or not anyone remembers, which is why remembering matters.
abstract.cn: 日期不管有没有人记得都会回来，所以「记得」才有意义。

abstract.en: Every anniversary is a small argument that the past still belongs to the present.
abstract.cn: 每个周年纪念都在小小地主张：过去仍属于现在。

examples.en: They mark their anniversary with a quiet walk by the river.
examples.cn: 他们以在河边安静散步的方式纪念结婚周年。

examples.en: The town is preparing for its two-hundredth anniversary.
examples.cn: 这座小镇正在筹备建镇两百周年纪念。

examples.en: On the anniversary of the fire, the church bells ring.
examples.cn: 在那场火灾的周年纪念日，教堂会鸣钟。

dict_mnemonic.text: 谐音「安尼窝舍瑞」：安尼每年都回那个小屋，纪念第一次见面的日子。

root: 拉丁语 annus（年）+ vertere（转动），anniversarius 即「每年转回来的」。

sensesIntro.en: The word names the returning date, the celebration held on it, and the numbered year that the returning has produced.
sensesIntro.cn: 这个词指每年返回的日期、当天的庆祝，以及一次次返回累积出的「第几年」。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a wheel of months turns once and stops on the same marked day.
core.cn: 核心意象：月份的轮子转完一圈，停在与去年相同的标记日。

branches.en: THE DATE: the first sense is the date itself coming back.
branches.cn: 日期线：第一个义项是日期本身又回来了。

branches.en: THE PARTY: the second sense is the gathering that makes the date public.
branches.cn: 庆典线：第二个义项是让日期公开可见的聚会。

branches.en: THE COUNT: the third sense is the number of turns so far.
branches.cn: 计数线：第三个义项是迄今为止转过的圈数。

branches.en: THE RETURN: private memory and public ceremony meet on one day.
branches.cn: 回返线：私人记忆与公开仪式在同一天相遇。

branches.en: THE NUMBER: a large count calls for a larger celebration.
branches.cn: 数字线：圈数越大，庆祝往往越大。

intro.en: The Latin year-root builds a family of time words, and English compounds mark kinds of anniversary.
intro.cn: 拉丁语「年」词根构成一族时间词，英语复合词则标示不同种类的周年。

latinIntro.en: Annus and anniversarius stand behind annual, annuity and anniversary; vertere supplies the turning image.
latinIntro.cn: annus 与 anniversarius 是 annual、annuity、anniversary 的基础；vertere 提供「转动」意象。

items.example: The annual report comes out in March.
items.exampleCN: 年度报告在三月发布。

items.example: The trees are inspected annually.
items.exampleCN: 这些树每年检查一次。

items.example: The annuity pays out every January.
items.exampleCN: 这笔年金每年一月支付。

items.example: The university celebrated its centenary.
items.exampleCN: 这所大学庆祝了建校百年。

items.example: The town planned a bicentennial parade.
items.exampleCN: 小镇筹划了一场两百周年游行。

items.meaning: a card sent to mark an anniversary
items.meaningCN: 为纪念周年寄出的卡片
items.example: She chose a funny anniversary card.
items.exampleCN: 她挑了一张有趣的周年贺卡。

items.example: They danced at their golden anniversary.
items.exampleCN: 他们在金婚纪念日跳舞。

items.meaning: a special edition issued for an anniversary
items.meaningCN: 为周年推出的特别版本
items.example: The publisher reissued an anniversary edition.
items.exampleCN: 出版社重新推出了周年纪念版。

definition_zh: 宣布；公布；播报；通报（客人到）；预示
definition_en: to tell people about something officially or publicly, or to make something known by signs
core_image: 一个人站到人群前面，提高声音，让消息一次传到所有耳朵里
scene: 礼堂里坐满了人，校长走上台，轻轻敲了敲麦克风。The principal announced the name of the winner.
sceneCN: 这里 announce 是「宣布」（第 1 个义项：公开告知众人）；句意为校长宣布了获胜者的名字。画面里有礼堂、讲台与麦克风。

pos.zh: 动词：宣布；公布；播报；通报
动词：作广播；通报来客

derivatives.zh: 由本词加 -ment 构成，义为「公告；宣布」
由本词加 -er 构成，义为「播音员；广播员」
由 un- 加 announced 构成，义为「未事先通知的」

senses.title: To make something known publicly
senses.titleCN: 宣布：公开告知众人
senses.definition: to tell a group of people about a fact, decision or plan in an official or public way
senses.definitionCN: 以正式或公开的方式向一群人告知事实、决定或计划
senses.example: The company announced a new policy on Monday.
senses.exampleCN: 公司在周一宣布了一项新政策。
senses.why: Latin nuntiare meant to bring news; announce is to carry a message out in front of everyone at once.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁语 nuntiare 意为「带来消息」，announce 就是把消息一次带到所有人面前。

senses.title: To read out over a broadcast
senses.titleCN: 播报：通过广播读出
senses.definition: to read information aloud to listeners or viewers, especially in radio, television or transport
senses.definitionCN: 向听众或观众朗读信息，尤用于广播、电视或交通播报
senses.example: The radio announced that the road was closed.
senses.exampleCN: 电台播报说那条路已封闭。
senses.why: Broadcasting repeats the ancient act at a distance: one voice reaches many rooms at once.
senses.whyCN: 广播把古老的动作拉到远处：一个声音同时抵达许多房间。

senses.title: To say that a guest has arrived
senses.titleCN: 通报：告知有客人到来
senses.definition: to tell someone, especially a person in a house or office, that a visitor has arrived
senses.definitionCN: 告知某人（尤指宅内或办公室内的人）有来访者到了
senses.example: The assistant announced the next visitor at the door.
senses.exampleCN: 助理在门口通报了下一位来访者。
senses.why: A servant once carried a name from the door to the master; the verb still keeps that short journey.
senses.whyCN: 从前仆人把名字从门口带到主人面前；这个动词仍保留着那段短短的行进。

senses.title: To be a sign of something
senses.titleCN: 预示：以迹象显示
senses.definition: to show clearly what is going to happen, often without words
senses.definitionCN: 以明显的方式显示将要发生的事，常无需言语
senses.example: The first frost announced that winter had come.
senses.exampleCN: 初霜预示着冬天已经到来。
senses.why: Signs are treated as messengers: the frost itself 'announces' what the season will bring.
senses.whyCN: 迹象被当作信使：霜本身就「宣布」季节将带来的东西。

intro.en: Announce comes from a Latin verb for bringing news, and it reached English through French.
intro.cn: announce 来自拉丁语表示「带来消息」的动词，经法语进入英语。

items.en: Nuntius meant 'messenger' or 'message', the person or thing that carried news.
items.cn: nuntius 意为「信使」或「消息」，即承载新闻的人或物。

items.en: Nuntiare meant 'to report, tell', the verb formed from the messenger word.
items.cn: nuntiare 意为「报告、告知」，是由「信使」一词构成的动词。

items.en: Ad- 'to' plus nuntiare gave annuntiare, 'to bring news to someone'.
items.cn: ad-「向」加 nuntiare 构成 annuntiare，即「把消息带给某人」。

items.en: Old French anoncier softened the Latin form and carried it toward English.
items.cn: 古法语 anoncier 软化了拉丁词形，并把它带向英语。

items.en: English adopted the verb in the fifteenth century; the spelling announce reflects later French influence.
items.cn: 英语在十五世纪采用这个动词；拼写 announce 反映了后来的法语影响。

items.en: Broadcasting and public relations widened the word, while the old sense of announcing a guest survives in formal households.
items.cn: 广播与公共关系拓宽了这个词，而「通报客人」的古义仍在正式场合保留。

note.en: The look-alike group is the announce family; the near-meaning group holds verbs of making something public.
note.cn: 形近组是 announce 词族；近义组收「使某事公开」的动词。

entries.definition: The noun for a public statement or the act of announcing.
entries.definitionCN: 指公开声明或宣布行为的名称。

entries.definition: A person who reads announcements on radio or television.
entries.definitionCN: 在广播或电视上播报的人。

entries.definition: Arriving or happening without warning.
entries.definitionCN: 未经预告就到来的。

entries.definition: To state something officially, often with legal or formal force.
entries.definitionCN: 正式声明，常带法律或正式效力。

entries.definition: To announce something publicly and with ceremony.
entries.definitionCN: 公开而隆重地宣布。

entries.definition: To give an account of something that has happened.
entries.definitionCN: 叙述已经发生的事。

entries.definition: To make something previously hidden visible.
entries.definitionCN: 使先前隐藏的事物显露。

normalIntro.en: These hooks link the word to the messenger root, to the stage, and to the difference between telling one person and telling a crowd.
normalIntro.cn: 下面几个钩子把这个词与「信使」词根、讲台，以及「告诉一个人」和「告诉一群人」的差别连起来。

normal.en: The root nunci- means messenger, and announce is to act as one in public.
normal.cn: 词根 nunci- 意为「信使」，announce 就是当众做信使。

normal.en: Say 'uh-NOUNCE': the stress is on the second beat, like a voice rising to be heard.
normal.cn: 读作「呃-NOUNCE」，重音在第二拍，像声音抬高以便被听见。

normal.en: Two n's: an-nounce, one from the prefix and one from the root.
normal.cn: 两个 n：an-nounce，一个来自前缀，一个来自词根。

normal.en: Announce is for crowds; tell is for one person; say is for anyone.
normal.cn: announce 面向人群，tell 面向一个人，say 面向任何人。

normal.en: The airport announces flights, the school announces winners, the frost announces winter.
normal.cn: 机场播报航班，学校宣布获奖者，霜则预示冬天。

abstract.en: To announce is to decide that a fact has become public property.
abstract.cn: 宣布就是决定某个事实从此成为公共财产。

abstract.en: Some things can only be announced once, and the word knows it.
abstract.cn: 有些事只能宣布一次，这个词明白这一点。

abstract.en: A true announcement asks the listeners to change their plans, not just their attention.
abstract.cn: 真正的宣布要求听众改变计划，而不只是改变注意力。

examples.en: They announced the engagement at a family dinner.
examples.cn: 他们在家庭聚餐上宣布了订婚。

examples.en: The station announced the delay over the loudspeaker.
examples.cn: 车站通过广播宣布了延误。

examples.en: A knock on the door announced her arrival before she spoke.
examples.cn: 她还没开口，敲门声就宣告了她的到来。

dict_mnemonic.text: 谐音「饿脑恩斯」：饿着脑子也要站起来，把消息大声宣布给大家。

root: 拉丁语 ad-（向）+ nuntiare（报告）+ nuntius（信使），原义「把消息带给某人」。

sensesIntro.en: The verb covers public statements, broadcast reading, the formal announcing of a guest, and signs that foretell events.
sensesIntro.cn: 这个动词覆盖公开声明、广播播报、正式通报来客，以及预示事件的迹象。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: one voice raised in front of many listeners, carrying a message to every ear at once.
core.cn: 核心意象：一个声音在许多听众面前抬高，把消息一次送到每只耳朵。

branches.en: THE STATEMENT: the first sense is an official public telling.
branches.cn: 声明线：第一个义项是正式的公开告知。

branches.en: THE BROADCAST: the second sense sends the voice through a machine.
branches.cn: 播报线：第二个义项让声音通过机器传出去。

branches.en: THE DOOR: the third sense is the short walk from visitor to host.
branches.cn: 门口线：第三个义项是从来客到主人之间那段短距离。

branches.en: THE SIGN: the fourth sense lets silent things act as messengers.
branches.cn: 迹象线：第四个义项让无声之物充当信使。

branches.en: THE MESSAGE: all three spoken senses move the same news to a listener.
branches.cn: 消息线：三个口头义项都在把同一条新闻送到听者那里。

intro.en: The verb takes -ment and -er, and un- negates the past participle.
intro.cn: 这个动词接 -ment 与 -er，un- 则否定过去分词。

latinIntro.en: Latin nuntiare and nuntius supply the stem; English adds its own suffixes around it.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 nuntiare 与 nuntius 提供词干，英语在其周围加上自己的后缀。

items.example: The announcement was met with applause.
items.exampleCN: 这项声明赢得了掌声。

items.example: The announcer read the scores clearly.
items.exampleCN: 播音员清楚地读出了比分。

items.example: He arrived unannounced at the office.
items.exampleCN: 他未打招呼就到了办公室。

items.example: The announced plan surprised no one.
items.exampleCN: 已公布的计划没人感到意外。

items.meaning: in the act of making public
items.example: The announcing voice was calm.
items.exampleCN: 播报的声音很平静。

items.example: They preannounce the sale each year.
items.exampleCN: 他们每年都提前公布促销。

items.example: The station reannounced the changed time.
items.exampleCN: 电台再次播报了更改的时间。

items.example: They publicly announce the results at noon.
items.exampleCN: 他们在正午公开宣布结果。

definition_zh: 公告；声明；宣布；通知；广播通知
definition_en: a public or official statement that gives information, or the act of making such a statement
core_image: 钉在公告板上的一张纸，字很大，谁走过都能看见
scene: 机场大厅的屏幕上跳出一行红字，旅客们纷纷抬头。The announcement told passengers that the flight was delayed.
sceneCN: 这里 announcement 是「通知、公告」（第 1 个义项：公开发布的信息）；句意为这则通知告知旅客航班延误。画面里有航班屏、行李箱与抬头的人群。

pos.zh: 名词：公告；声明；宣布；通知

derivatives.zh: 本词的动词形式，义为「宣布；播报」
由动词加 -er 构成，义为「播音员」
由 un- 加 announced 构成，义为「未通知的」

senses.title: A public statement of information
senses.titleCN: 公告：公开发布的信息
senses.definition: a public or official statement that gives people information they need or want
senses.definitionCN: 向公众或正式发布、提供人们所需或想知道的信息的声明
senses.example: The school posted an announcement about the new timetable.
senses.exampleCN: 学校发布了关于新课程表的公告。
senses.why: The noun is the message itself, left standing after the voice has stopped so that later readers can still receive it.
senses.whyCN: 名词就是消息本身：声音停下后它仍留在那里，让后来的读者仍能收到。

senses.title: The act of announcing
senses.titleCN: 宣布：发布这一行为
senses.definition: the act or occasion of making something known publicly
senses.definitionCN: 把某事公开告知的行为或场合
senses.example: Her announcement of the winner was met with silence.
senses.exampleCN: 她宣布获胜者时，现场一片沉默。
senses.why: The same word names the act and its product, as English often does with -ment nouns.
senses.whyCN: 同一个词既指行为也指产物，英语中带 -ment 的名词常有这种双重性。

senses.title: A broadcast notice
senses.titleCN: 广播通知：交通或场所的即时播报
senses.definition: a short notice read aloud in an airport, station or other public place
senses.definitionCN: 在机场、车站或其他公共场所朗读的简短通知
senses.example: A last-minute announcement changed the boarding gate.
senses.exampleCN: 一则临时通知更改了登机口。
senses.why: Public places repeat the message aloud because not everyone can read the same board at the same moment.
senses.whyCN: 公共场所把消息反复读出来，因为并非每个人都能在同一刻读到同一块牌子。

intro.en: Announcement is the noun built on announce, whose Latin root means messenger.
intro.cn: announcement 是建立在 announce 之上的名词，其拉丁词根意为「信使」。

items.en: Nuntius meant 'messenger, message', the source of the whole family.
items.cn: nuntius 意为「信使、消息」，是整个词族的源头。

items.en: Annuntiare meant 'to bring news to', built with ad- 'to' and nuntiare 'report'.
items.cn: annuntiare 意为「把消息带给」，由 ad-「向」与 nuntiare「报告」构成。

items.en: Old French carried the verb toward English, where it became announce.
items.cn: 古法语把这个动词带向英语，在那里变成 announce。

items.en: The verb appears in fifteenth-century English; the noun announcement follows later.
items.cn: 动词见于十五世纪英语，名词 announcement 稍后出现。

items.en: The suffix -ment turns the act into a thing: the announcing becomes an announcement one can hold or read.
items.cn: 后缀 -ment 把行为变成事物：宣布变成了可以拿在手里或阅读的公告。

items.en: Print, radio and airports made the noun a daily object rather than a rare ceremony.
items.cn: 印刷、广播与机场让这个名词成为日常物件，而不再是稀有的仪式。

note.en: The look-alike group is the announce family; the near-meaning group holds kinds of public notice.
note.cn: 形近组是 announce 词族；近义组收各类公开通告。

entries.definition: The verb meaning to make something known publicly.
entries.definitionCN: 动词，义为「公开宣布」。

entries.definition: A person who reads announcements aloud.
entries.definitionCN: 朗读公告的人。

entries.definition: Not preceded by any announcement.
entries.definitionCN: 事先没有任何通知的。

entries.definition: Something said or written formally to make a position clear.
entries.definitionCN: 为表明立场而正式说出或写下的内容。

entries.definition: A short written sign or warning giving information.
entries.definitionCN: 提供信息的简短书面告示或警告。

entries.definition: A short official news report or update.
entries.definitionCN: 简短的官方新闻报告或最新消息。

entries.definition: A formal and often official statement.
entries.definitionCN: 正式且常具官方性质的声明。

normalIntro.en: These hooks connect the noun to its verb, to the -ment that makes it a thing, and to the airport board.
normalIntro.cn: 下面几个钩子把这个名词与它的动词、把它变成「东西」的 -ment，以及机场告示牌连起来。

normal.en: Announce plus ment: the act becomes an object you can read.
normal.cn: announce 加 ment：行为变成了可以阅读的物件。

normal.en: Say 'uh-NOUNS-munt': four syllables, the stress still on the second.
normal.cn: 读作「呃-NOUNS-门特」，四个音节，重音仍在第二。

normal.en: Picture a sheet of paper on a board, corners curled from being read.
normal.cn: 想象公告板上的一张纸，四角因被人反复阅读而卷起。

normal.en: Make an announcement is the standard verb phrase; the noun does not take 'do'.
normal.cn: 标准说法是 make an announcement，这个名词不搭配 do。

normal.en: The plural announcements is regular, and public places make many of them.
normal.cn: 复数 announcements 规则变化，公共场所每天都在发很多条。

abstract.en: An announcement is a fact that has been given a public address.
abstract.cn: 公告就是一个被赋予公共地址的事实。

abstract.en: The word assumes a listener who was not there when the news was first known.
abstract.cn: 这个词预设了一位听众：消息最初被知道时，他并不在场。

abstract.en: Some announcements inform, and some simply make the speaker feel official.
abstract.cn: 有些公告是在告知，有些只是让发布者觉得自己很正式。

examples.en: The announcement was pinned to the door of the office.
examples.cn: 公告被钉在办公室的门上。

examples.en: We waited in the hall for an announcement about the results.
examples.cn: 我们在大厅等待关于结果的公告。

examples.en: Her sudden announcement surprised even her closest friends.
examples.cn: 她突然的宣布连最亲近的朋友都吃了一惊。

dict_mnemonic.text: 谐音「饿脑斯门特」：饿着脑子也要把公告贴到门上，让所有人都看见。

root: 由 announce（拉丁语 ad- 向 + nuntiare 报告）加名词后缀 -ment 构成，指「发布出来的消息」。

sensesIntro.en: The noun names the published message, the act of publishing it, and the short broadcast notice of everyday public life.
sensesIntro.cn: 这个名词既指发布出来的消息，也指发布行为，还指日常公共生活中的简短广播通知。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a large printed sheet fixed where everyone who passes must see it.
core.cn: 核心意象：一张大字印刷的纸，固定在每个路过者都会看见的地方。

branches.en: THE SHEET: the first sense is the message as a public object.
branches.cn: 纸面线：第一个义项是作为公共物件的消息。

branches.en: THE ACT: the second sense is the moment of making it public.
branches.cn: 行为线：第二个义项是使其公开的那一刻。

branches.en: THE LOUDSPEAKER: the third sense is the short spoken notice in a public place.
branches.cn: 广播线：第三个义项是公共场所的简短口头通知。

branches.en: THE REACH: written and spoken forms exist to reach people who were not present.
branches.cn: 触达线：书面与口头形式都是为了触达当时不在场的人。

branches.en: THE DUALITY: the word names both the thing and the doing.
branches.cn: 双重线：这个词同时命名事物与行为。

intro.en: The noun sits at the centre of a small family built on -ment, -er and un-.
intro.cn: 这个名词处在一个小词族的中心，词族由 -ment、-er 与 un- 构成。

latinIntro.en: The Latin stem nunti- carries the messenger idea; English suffixes build the noun and the person.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁词干 nunti- 承载「信使」观念，英语后缀构成名词与人物。

items.example: They announce the winners at noon.
items.exampleCN: 他们在正午宣布获胜者。

items.example: The announcer repeated the gate number.
items.exampleCN: 播音员重复了登机口号码。

items.example: An unannounced visitor rang the bell.
items.exampleCN: 一位未预约的访客按了门铃。

items.meaningCN: 面向所有人发布的公告
items.example: The public announcement was posted online.
items.exampleCN: 公开声明发布在网上。

items.example: An official announcement followed the meeting.
items.exampleCN: 会议之后发布了官方公告。

items.example: The flight announcement listed the new gate.
items.exampleCN: 航班通知列出了新的登机口。

items.meaning: a public notice of a marriage
items.example: They sent a wedding announcement to the paper.
items.exampleCN: 他们向报社寄了婚礼公告。

items.meaning: a board where notices are displayed
items.example: The announcement board was full of notices.
items.exampleCN: 公告板上贴满了通知。

definition_zh: 使恼怒；使烦恼；打扰；骚扰
definition_en: to make someone feel slightly angry or irritated, especially by repeated or unwanted action
core_image: 一只小虫绕着耳朵转个不停，赶走了又回来
scene: 图书馆里有人反复翻动塑料袋，邻座的人皱起眉头。The rustling bag began to annoy everyone at the table.
sceneCN: 这里 annoy 是「使恼怒、使烦恼」（第 1 个义项：使人产生轻微愤怒）；句意为那只沙沙作响的袋子开始让桌边所有人烦起来。画面里有图书馆、塑料袋与皱眉的读者。

pos.zh: 动词：使恼怒；使烦恼；打扰

derivatives.zh: 由本词加 -ance 构成，义为「恼怒；烦扰」
由本词加 -ing 构成，义为「令人恼火的」
annoying 加 -ly 构成，义为「恼人地」
由本词加 -ed 构成，义为「感到恼火的」

senses.title: To make someone slightly angry
senses.titleCN: 使恼怒：让人产生轻微愤怒
senses.definition: to make a person feel slightly angry or irritated
senses.definitionCN: 使一个人感到轻微愤怒或不快
senses.example: His constant questions began to annoy her.
senses.exampleCN: 他没完没了的问题开始惹恼她。
senses.why: Old French anuier meant to trouble or harm; annoy is the mild modern form of that old trouble.
senses.whyCN: 古法语 anuier 意为「烦扰、损害」，annoy 是那份古老烦扰在现代的轻度版本。

senses.title: To disturb someone repeatedly
senses.titleCN: 打扰：反复干扰使人不得安宁
senses.definition: to keep disturbing a person with unwanted actions, sounds or requests
senses.definitionCN: 以不受欢迎的动作、声音或请求反复干扰某人
senses.example: The flies annoyed the horses all afternoon.
senses.exampleCN: 苍蝇整个下午都在骚扰那些马。
senses.why: The word often implies repetition: one small thing is bearable, but the same thing again and again wears a person down.
senses.whyCN: 这个词常含重复意味：一件小事尚可忍受，但同一件事反复出现就会把人磨垮。

senses.title: To cause mild discomfort to a part of the body
senses.titleCN: 使不适：轻微刺激身体某处
senses.definition: to cause slight pain or irritation to a part of the body
senses.definitionCN: 使身体某处产生轻微疼痛或刺激感
senses.example: The rough collar annoyed his neck.
senses.exampleCN: 粗糙的衣领磨得他脖子不舒服。
senses.why: The same mild trouble can be caused by a thing rather than a person; the body is irritated the way a mind is.
senses.whyCN: 同样的轻度烦扰也可以由物而非人造成；身体被刺激，正如心情被刺激。

intro.en: Annoy came through Old French from a Latin phrase meaning 'to be hateful to'.
intro.cn: annoy 经古法语来自一个拉丁语短语，意为「对……是可恨的」。

items.en: The phrase in odio esse meant 'to be an object of hatred', built on odium 'hatred'.
items.cn: 短语 in odio esse 意为「成为憎恨的对象」，由 odium「憎恨」构成。

items.en: Old French anuier meant 'to trouble, harm, vex', a much stronger word than modern annoy.
items.cn: 古法语 anuier 意为「烦扰、损害、使恼」，比现代 annoy 重得多。

items.en: Middle English annoy could still mean serious harm, not only mild irritation.
items.cn: 中古英语 annoy 仍可指严重损害，而不只是轻微不快。

items.en: By the early modern period the word had softened to the everyday sense of irritating someone.
items.cn: 到近代早期，这个词已软化为日常的「惹人烦」。

items.en: The noun annoyance and the adjective annoying grew beside the verb, covering feeling and cause.
items.cn: 名词 annoyance 与形容词 annoying 在动词旁生长，分别覆盖感受与成因。

note.en: The look-alike group is the annoy family; the near-meaning group moves from mild irritation to deliberate pestering.
note.cn: 形近组是 annoy 词族；近义组从轻微刺激一路排到故意纠缠。

entries.definition: The feeling of being annoyed, or something that causes it.
entries.definitionCN: 被惹恼的感受，或引起这种感受的事物。

entries.definition: Causing slight anger or irritation.
entries.definitionCN: 引起轻微愤怒或不快的。

entries.definition: Feeling slight anger about something.
entries.definitionCN: 因某事而感到微微恼火的。

entries.definition: To make someone mildly angry, often by a repeated action.
entries.definitionCN: 使某人轻度生气，常因反复的动作。

entries.definition: To disturb or trouble someone, often with a request.
entries.definitionCN: 打扰或烦扰某人，常带请求。

entries.definition: To interrupt someone's peace, work or sleep.
entries.definitionCN: 打断某人的安宁、工作或睡眠。

entries.definition: To keep annoying someone with repeated requests.
entries.definitionCN: 以反复请求不断纠缠某人。

normalIntro.en: These hooks link the word to the insect image, to its French softening, and to the difference between mild and repeated trouble.
normalIntro.cn: 下面几个钩子把这个词与「小虫」意象、法语来源的软化，以及「轻微」与「反复」的差别连起来。

normal.en: Say 'uh-NOY': it rhymes with boy, and a persistent boy at the door is the right picture.
normal.cn: 读作「呃-NOY」，与 boy 押韵；门口赖着不走的小男孩正是那个画面。

normal.en: The two n's come from the prefix and the root: an-noy.
normal.cn: 两个 n 分别来自前缀与词根：an-noy。

normal.en: Old French meant harm; modern English means mild irritation, so the word has cooled over time.
normal.cn: 古法语意为伤害；现代英语意为轻微不快，这个词随时间冷却了。

normal.en: Annoy is the verb, annoyed the feeling, annoying the cause, annoyance the whole state.
normal.cn: annoy 是动作，annoyed 是感受，annoying 是成因，annoyance 是整体状态。

normal.en: A fly is annoying; a swarm of flies is unbearable.
normal.cn: 一只苍蝇惹人烦，一群苍蝇就让人受不了。

abstract.en: Annoyance is the tax paid for being near other people.
abstract.cn: 烦恼是靠近他人所缴的税。

abstract.en: The word is mild on purpose: it names the thousand small frictions that never quite become anger.
abstract.cn: 这个词故意很轻：它命名了千百次从未真正变成愤怒的小摩擦。

abstract.en: What annoys us often reveals what we cannot control.
abstract.cn: 惹恼我们的事，常暴露我们无法掌控的东西。

examples.en: Please turn the music down; it annoys the neighbours.
examples.cn: 请把音乐关小一点，它吵得邻居很烦。

examples.en: She was annoyed that no one had told her about the change.
examples.cn: 她因没人告诉她这项变动而恼火。

examples.en: The delay annoyed him more than the heat.
examples.cn: 延误比炎热更让他心烦。

dict_mnemonic.text: 谐音「额闹伊」：额头上嗡嗡闹个不停的蚊子，真让人恼火。

root: 古法语 anuier（烦扰、损害），源自拉丁语短语 in odio esse（成为憎恨的对象）。

sensesIntro.en: The word covers mild anger, repeated disturbance and slight physical irritation, all forms of small persistent trouble.
sensesIntro.cn: 这个词覆盖轻微愤怒、反复干扰与轻微的身体刺激，都是小而持续的烦扰。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a small insect circles a person's ear and returns each time it is waved away.
core.cn: 核心意象：一只小虫绕着人的耳朵转，每次被赶走又飞回来。

branches.en: THE FEELING: the first sense is the mild anger produced in a person.
branches.cn: 感受线：第一个义项是被造成的那种轻微愤怒。

branches.en: THE REPETITION: the second sense is the repeated disturbance that produces it.
branches.cn: 反复线：第二个义项是产生这种感受的反复干扰。

branches.en: THE BODY: the third sense transfers the same friction to skin or clothing.
branches.cn: 身体线：第三个义项把同样的摩擦转到皮肤或衣物上。

branches.en: THE WEAR: annoyance is what repetition does to patience.
branches.cn: 磨损线：烦恼就是重复对耐心所做的磨损。

branches.en: THE ANALOGY: an irritated mind and an irritated neck work the same way.
branches.cn: 类比线：被惹恼的心与被磨的脖子运作方式相同。

intro.en: The family adds -ance, -ing, -ed and -ly to name the state, the cause, the feeling and the manner.
intro.cn: 这个词族加 -ance、-ing、-ed、-ly，分别命名状态、成因、感受与方式。

latinIntro.en: The Old French stem anui- comes from Latin odium 'hatred'; English suffixes do the rest.
latinIntro.cn: 古法语词干 anui- 来自拉丁语 odium「憎恨」，其余由英语后缀完成。

items.meaning: the state of being annoyed or its cause
items.meaningCN: 被惹恼的状态或其成因
items.example: He could not hide his annoyance.
items.exampleCN: 他掩饰不住自己的恼火。

items.example: That beeping sound is really annoying.
items.exampleCN: 那个滴滴声真让人烦。

items.example: Annoyingly, the train left a minute early.
items.exampleCN: 恼人的是，火车早开了一分钟。

items.example: She looked annoyed but said nothing.
items.exampleCN: 她看起来有点恼火，却什么也没说。

items.meaning: one who or that which annoys
items.example: The mosquito is a perfect annoyer.
items.exampleCN: 蚊子是完美的扰人者。

items.example: Tapping his pen is an annoying habit.
items.exampleCN: 敲笔是他一个惹人烦的习惯。

items.example: The annoying noise came from the old fan.
items.exampleCN: 那恼人的噪音来自旧风扇。

items.meaning: a wait that makes people impatient
items.example: An annoying delay kept them two hours.
items.exampleCN: 一场恼人的延误让他们耽搁了两小时。

definition_zh: 每年的；年度的；一年一度的；一年生的；（名词）年刊
definition_en: happening once every year, calculated over a year, or living for only one year
core_image: 日历翻过最后一页，同一件事又在下一年的同一格等着
scene: 岁末的办公室里，会计翻着一摞刚打印好的报表。The annual report arrived at the end of every year.
sceneCN: 这里 annual 是「年度的」（第 1 个义项：按一年计算的）；句意为年度报告每年年底送达。画面里有报表、订书机与日历。

pos.zh: 形容词：每年的；年度的；一年生的
名词：年刊；年鉴；一年生植物

derivatives.zh: 由本词加 -ly 构成，义为「每年；一年一次地」
由同一拉丁词根 annus 加 -ity 构成，义为「年金」
由本词加 -ize 与 -ed 构成，义为「按年折算的」

senses.title: Calculated or happening over a year
senses.titleCN: 年度的：按一年计算的
senses.definition: calculated over a period of one year, or relating to a whole year
senses.definitionCN: 按一年期间计算的，或与整年相关的
senses.example: The family's annual income has barely changed.
senses.exampleCN: 这个家庭的年收入几乎没有变化。
senses.why: Latin annus meant year, so annual simply marks the unit of one full turn of the calendar.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁语 annus 意为「年」，annual 只是标示日历转满一圈这个单位。

senses.title: Happening once every year
senses.titleCN: 一年一度的：每年发生一次
senses.definition: happening once each year, often as a regular event
senses.definitionCN: 每年发生一次，常指固定的例行事
senses.example: The annual festival fills the square every June.
senses.exampleCN: 一年一度的节庆每年六月挤满广场。
senses.why: The same unit becomes a rhythm: one event per turn of the year.
senses.whyCN: 同一个单位变成了节奏：每转一年发生一件事。

senses.title: Living for one year, of a plant
senses.titleCN: 一年生的：生命周期为一年的植物
senses.definition: of a plant, completing its life cycle within a single year
senses.definitionCN: 指植物在一年之内完成整个生命周期
senses.example: Marigolds are annual plants in this climate.
senses.exampleCN: 在这种气候下，万寿菊是一年生植物。
senses.why: The calendar unit is applied to a life span: the plant's whole life fits inside one year.
senses.whyCN: 日历单位被用到了寿命上：这株植物的整个生命正好装进一年。

senses.title: A yearly publication
senses.titleCN: 年刊：每年出版一期的出版物
senses.definition: a book, magazine or report published once a year
senses.definitionCN: 每年出版一期的书、杂志或报告
senses.example: She keeps every annual of the photography club.
senses.exampleCN: 她保存着摄影俱乐部的每一本年刊。
senses.why: The adjective becomes a noun for the thing that appears once per year, a common English shortcut.
senses.whyCN: 形容词转作名词，指每年出现一次的东西，这是英语常见的省略说法。

intro.en: Annual comes from the Latin word for year, and its family includes annuity and anniversary.
intro.cn: annual 来自拉丁语中表示「年」的词，其词族还包括 annuity 与 anniversary。

items.en: Annus meant 'year', and it stands behind annual, annuity and anniversary.
items.cn: annus 意为「年」，是 annual、annuity、anniversary 的共同来源。

items.en: Annuus was the adjective 'yearly', formed directly from annus.
items.cn: annuus 是由 annus 直接构成的形容词，意为「每年的」。

items.en: Annalis meant 'relating to a year', and it also gave the English annals, a yearly record.
items.cn: annalis 意为「与年相关的」，也生出英语 annals，即编年记录。

items.en: Old French annuel carried the adjective into English with the sense of yearly.
items.cn: 古法语 annuel 把这个形容词带入英语，意为「每年的」。

items.en: English adopted the word in the fifteenth century; the exact first record is uncertain.
items.cn: 英语在十五世纪采用这个词，确切的首条记录不确定。

items.en: Business, botany and publishing each gave the word a special use: reports, plants and yearbooks.
items.cn: 商业、植物学与出版业各自给了这个词特殊用法：年报、一年生植物与年刊。

note.en: The look-alike group shares the Latin year-root; the near-meaning group names other repeated or seasonal cycles.
note.cn: 形近组共享拉丁语「年」词根；近义组收其他周期与季节性的说法。

entries.definition: The adverb meaning once a year.
entries.definitionCN: 副词，义为「每年一次」。

entries.definition: A yearly payment, often for life.
entries.definitionCN: 按年支付的款项，常为终身。

entries.definition: The yearly return of a memorable date.
entries.definitionCN: 值得纪念的日期每年返回。

entries.definition: Happening or produced once every year.
entries.definitionCN: 每年发生或产出一次的。

entries.definition: Of a plant, living for several years; also lasting a long time.
entries.definitionCN: 指植物活多年，也指持续很久的。

entries.definition: Happening once every month.
entries.definitionCN: 每月发生一次的。

entries.definition: Happening again, often at regular intervals.
entries.definitionCN: 再次发生的，常按固定间隔。

normalIntro.en: These hooks use the year-root, the -al ending, and the picture of a calendar completing its circle.
normalIntro.cn: 下面几个钩子用到「年」词根、-al 结尾，以及日历走完一圈的画面。

normal.en: Ann- means year, so annual is the adjective of the year.
normal.cn: ann- 表示年，所以 annual 就是「年的」形容词。

normal.en: Say 'AN-yoo-ul': three beats, with the stress on the first.
normal.cn: 读作「AN-优-欧」，三拍，重音在第一拍。

normal.en: Annual is the adjective; annually is the adverb; annuity is the money paid each year.
normal.cn: annual 是形容词，annually 是副词，annuity 是每年支付的钱。

normal.en: An annual plant lives one year; a perennial comes back.
normal.cn: 一年生植物只活一年，多年生植物会回来。

normal.en: The annual report is the report that closes the year.
normal.cn: 年度报告就是给一年收尾的那份报告。

abstract.en: The year is the unit by which institutions pretend time is tidy.
abstract.cn: 「年」是机构用来假装时间很整齐的单位。

abstract.en: An annual event is a promise made to the future by the past.
abstract.cn: 一年一度的活动，是过去对未来作出的承诺。

abstract.en: Counting years is one of the oldest ways humans turn change into a story.
abstract.cn: 数年是人类把变化变成故事的最古老方式之一。

examples.en: The company holds an annual meeting in spring.
examples.cn: 公司在春天举行年度会议。

examples.en: Annual rainfall has fallen for three years.
examples.cn: 年降雨量已经连续三年下降。

examples.en: These flowers are annuals and must be replanted each year.
examples.cn: 这些花是一年生植物，每年都要重新栽种。

dict_mnemonic.text: 谐音「安牛儿」：安家的牛儿每年只干一次重活，就是年度大扫除。

root: 拉丁语 annus（年）→ annuus（每年的），经古法语 annuel 进入英语。

sensesIntro.en: The word covers yearly calculation, yearly recurrence, a one-year plant life, and the publication that appears each year.
sensesIntro.cn: 这个词覆盖按年计算、每年重现、一年生植物的寿命，以及每年出版一期的刊物。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a calendar circle closes and the same mark waits in the same square next year.
core.cn: 核心意象：日历的圆走满一圈，同一个标记在下一年同一格里等着。

branches.en: THE TOTAL: the first sense measures something across a full year.
branches.cn: 总量线：第一个义项把某物按整年计量。

branches.en: THE RHYTHM: the second sense is one event per year.
branches.cn: 节奏线：第二个义项是每年一次的事件。

branches.en: THE LIFE: the third sense applies the year to a plant's whole span.
branches.cn: 生命线：第三个义项把一年用在植物的整个寿命上。

branches.en: THE VOLUME: the fourth sense is the object published once a year.
branches.cn: 卷册线：第四个义项是每年出版一次的物件。

branches.en: THE UNIT: measurement and recurrence are the same year seen two ways.
branches.cn: 单位线：计量与重现是同一个「年」的两种看法。

intro.en: The year-root takes -ly, -ity and -ized, and compounds name reports, meetings and plants.
intro.cn: 「年」词根接 -ly、-ity、-ized，复合词则命名报告、会议与植物。

latinIntro.en: Latin annus gives annual; annuus gives the adjective, and annus plus -ity gives annuity.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 annus 生出 annual；annuus 提供形容词，annus 加 -ity 则成 annuity。

items.example: The bridge is inspected annually.
items.exampleCN: 这座桥每年检查一次。

items.example: The annuity begins at retirement.
items.exampleCN: 年金从退休时开始支付。

items.meaning: calculated as if for a full year
items.example: The annualized rate was six percent.
items.exampleCN: 年化比率为百分之六。

items.example: The annual report was late again.
items.exampleCN: 年度报告又迟了。

items.meaning: a meeting held once a year
items.example: Shareholders attend the annual meeting.
items.exampleCN: 股东参加年度会议。

items.example: Her annual income doubled in five years.
items.exampleCN: 她的年收入五年间翻了一倍。

items.meaning: a plant that completes its life in one year
items.meaningCN: 一年内完成生命周期的植物
items.example: The garden is full of annual plants.
items.exampleCN: 园子里种满了一年生的植物。

items.meaning: paid holiday days allowed each year
items.meaningCN: 每年可享有的带薪假期
items.example: He saved his annual leave for summer.
items.exampleCN: 他把年假留到夏天用。

definition_zh: 另一个；再一个；又一个；另外的
definition_en: one more person or thing of the same kind, or a different one
core_image: 同样的杯子又出现一只，排在刚才那只旁边
scene: 桌上的一杯茶喝完了，客人把空杯往前推了推。She poured another cup and handed it to him.
sceneCN: 这里 another 是「再一个、另一个」（第 1 个义项：同类中再加一个）；句意为她又倒了一杯递给他。画面里有茶壶、空杯与桌面。

pos.zh: 限定词：另一个；再一个
代词：另一个（人或物）

derivatives.zh: 同源词，义为「其他的」，与 another 共享古英语 ōþer 词根
由 other 加 -wise 构成，义为「否则；在其他方面」
由 other 加 -ness 构成，义为「他异性；不同之处」

senses.title: One more of the same kind
senses.titleCN: 再一个：同类中再加一个
senses.definition: one additional person or thing of the same kind as the one already mentioned
senses.definitionCN: 与已提到的同类中再增加一个人或物
senses.example: Would you like another biscuit?
senses.exampleCN: 你想再来一块饼干吗？
senses.why: The word is literally 'an other': one more instance drawn from the same set.
senses.whyCN: 这个词字面上就是「一个别的」，即从同一集合里再取一个。

senses.title: A further amount of time or quantity
senses.titleCN: 再：数量或时间上再加一段
senses.definition: used before a number or amount to mean an additional stretch of it
senses.definitionCN: 用在数字或数量前，表示再加一段
senses.example: The trip will take another three days.
senses.exampleCN: 这趟旅行还要再花三天。
senses.why: Counting continues past the first total: one more unit is added to the number already reached.
senses.whyCN: 计数越过第一个总数继续走：在已达的数字上再加一个单位。

senses.title: A different one
senses.titleCN: 另一个：不同于此前的那个
senses.definition: a different person or thing, not the one already known or chosen
senses.definitionCN: 与已知或已选的那个不同的人或物
senses.example: That is another question entirely.
senses.exampleCN: 那完全是另一个问题。
senses.why: The same form can shift from 'one more' to 'a different one', because both mean the next item on the other side of this one.
senses.whyCN: 同一形式可以从「再加一个」滑向「另一个不同的」，因为两者都指此物另一边的下一项。

intro.en: Another began as two words, 'an other', and English speakers fused them into one.
intro.cn: another 起初是两个词「an other」，说英语的人把它们合成一个。

items.en: An was the numeral 'one', the ancestor of the modern indefinite article a and an.
items.cn: an 是数词「一」，是现代不定冠词 a 与 an 的祖先。

items.en: Ōþer meant 'other, second', and it is the source of modern other.
items.cn: ōþer 意为「别的、第二个」，是现代 other 的来源。

items.en: The phrase an other was written as two words, and in speech the boundary between them blurred.
items.cn: 短语 an other 原写作两个词，口语中两者之间的界限变得模糊。

items.en: Writers eventually joined the two into the single word another, and the n stayed in place.
items.cn: 作者最终把两者合为一个词 another，其中的 n 保留了下来。

items.en: The word now serves both as a determiner and as a pronoun, covering 'one more' and 'a different one'.
items.cn: 这个词如今既作限定词也作代词，覆盖「再来一个」与「另一个不同的」。

note.en: The look-alike group is the other family; the near-meaning group holds words for one more or a different item.
note.cn: 形近组是 other 词族；近义组收表示「再加一个」或「另一个」的词。

entries.definition: The adjective for a different person or thing.
entries.definitionCN: 表示「另一个、其他的」的形容词。

entries.definition: In different circumstances, or in other respects.
entries.definitionCN: 在不同情况下，或在其他方面。

entries.definition: The quality of being different from what is familiar.
entries.definitionCN: 与熟悉事物不同的性质。

entries.definition: Extra, added to what already exists.
entries.definitionCN: 额外的，加在已有事物之上的。

entries.definition: More than the usual or expected amount.
entries.definitionCN: 超出通常或预期数量的。

entries.definition: Additional, especially in distance or degree.
entries.definitionCN: 进一步的，尤指距离或程度上。

entries.definition: Coming after the first in order.
entries.definitionCN: 顺序上排在第一个之后的。

normalIntro.en: These hooks use the 'an other' origin, the fixed spelling, and the picture of a second cup.
normalIntro.cn: 下面几个钩子用到「an other」的来源、固定拼写，以及「第二只杯子」的画面。

normal.en: Another is 'an other' written as one word; the n belongs to the article.
normal.cn: another 就是写成一词的 an other；那个 n 属于冠词。

normal.en: Say 'uh-NUTH-er': the th is voiced, like the th in brother.
normal.cn: 读作「呃-NUTH-尔」，th 是浊音，像 brother 里的 th。

normal.en: Another is singular: another book, not another books.
normal.cn: another 接单数：another book，而不是 another books。

normal.en: Another three days means three more days, not a different three days.
normal.cn: another three days 意为「再三天」，不是「另外那三天」。

normal.en: One another and each other both mean mutual action.
normal.cn: one another 与 each other 都表示相互动作。

abstract.en: Another is the word that keeps a series open.
abstract.cn: another 是让序列保持敞开的那个词。

abstract.en: Saying another implies there is still room in the set.
abstract.cn: 说 another 意味着这个集合里还有位置。

abstract.en: The word can mean repetition or difference, and only context decides which.
abstract.cn: 这个词可以表示重复，也可以表示差异，只有语境能决定。

examples.en: He stayed another week in the village.
examples.cn: 他在村里又待了一周。

examples.en: This pen is broken; give me another.
examples.cn: 这支笔坏了，给我另一支。

examples.en: They sat in silence, looking at one another.
examples.cn: 他们静静地坐着，彼此对视。

dict_mnemonic.text: 谐音「阿那泽」：阿那泽又端来一个，说「另一个也给你」。

root: 古英语 an（一）+ ōþer（别的、第二个），两个词在书面语中合并为 another。

sensesIntro.en: The word adds one more of the same kind, adds an amount of time or number, and marks a different item.
sensesIntro.cn: 这个词表示同类中再加一个、再加一段数量或时间，以及标示另一个不同的事物。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a second identical cup is set down beside the first.
core.cn: 核心意象：第二只一模一样的杯子被放在第一只旁边。

branches.en: THE SECOND CUP: the first sense is one more of the same kind.
branches.cn: 第二杯线：第一个义项是同类中再加一个。

branches.en: THE EXTRA STRETCH: the second sense adds time or amount.
branches.cn: 加段线：第二个义项增加时间或数量。

branches.en: THE DIFFERENT ONE: the third sense points to an item unlike this one.
branches.cn: 异项线：第三个义项指向与此不同的那一项。

branches.en: THE ADDITION: both meanings add something to what is already counted.
branches.cn: 添加线：两种含义都在已有计数上再加东西。

branches.en: THE OPEN SET: repetition and difference are two edges of the same open series.
branches.cn: 开放线：重复与差异是同一个开放序列的两端。

intro.en: Another does not take affixes, but its root other builds a family and fixed phrases.
intro.cn: another 本身不接词缀，但其词根 other 构成词族与固定短语。

latinIntro.en: The word is Germanic, not Latin; the family is built with -wise, -ness and reciprocal phrases.
latinIntro.cn: 这个词属日耳曼语而非拉丁语；词族用 -wise、-ness 与相互短语构成。

items.example: The other door was locked.
items.exampleCN: 另一扇门锁着。

items.example: Hurry, otherwise we will be late.
items.exampleCN: 快点，否则我们要迟到了。

items.example: The story explores otherness in a small town.
items.exampleCN: 这个故事探讨小镇中的他异性。

items.example: They help one another with the work.
items.exampleCN: 他们互相帮忙做这份工作。

items.example: The two teams know each other well.
items.exampleCN: 这两支队伍彼此很熟。

items.example: This one is cold; I will take another one.
items.exampleCN: 这个凉了，我要另一个。

items.example: Yet another meeting was scheduled.
items.exampleCN: 又安排了一场会议。

items.example: There must be another way to solve this.
items.exampleCN: 解决这个问题一定还有另一种办法。

definition_zh: 回答；答案；答复；回信；应门；接听；符合；答辩
definition_en: something said or written in reply to a question, or the act of replying to a question, call or need
core_image: 问题像一扇敲响的门，回应是把门打开
scene: 教室里老师刚提问，前排的男孩就举起了手。He answered the question without looking at his notes.
sceneCN: 这里 answer 是「回答」（第 1 个义项：用言语回应问题）；句意为他没看笔记就回答了这个问题。画面里有教室、讲台与举手的学生。

pos.zh: 名词：回答；答案；答复
动词：回答；答复；应门；符合

derivatives.zh: 由本词加 -able 构成，义为「可回答的；负有责任的」
由本词加 -er 构成，义为「回答者」
由 un- 加 answered 构成，义为「未获答复的」

senses.title: A spoken reply to a question
senses.titleCN: 回答：对问题的口头回应
senses.definition: words spoken or written in reply to a question
senses.definitionCN: 为回应问题而说出或写下的内容
senses.example: Her answer was short and clear.
senses.exampleCN: 她的回答简短而清楚。
senses.why: Old English andswaru was a 'swearing against', a formal reply made in the face of a charge.
senses.whyCN: 古英语 andswaru 是「对着起誓」，指面对指控时作出的正式回应。

senses.title: The correct solution
senses.titleCN: 答案：问题的正确解答
senses.definition: the correct response to a problem or test question
senses.definitionCN: 对问题或试题的正确回应
senses.example: The answer to the last question was wrong.
senses.exampleCN: 最后一题的答案是错的。
senses.why: A reply is judged against a standard, and the reply that meets it becomes the answer key.
senses.whyCN: 回答要被标准衡量，符合标准的那个回答就成了标准答案。

senses.title: A written reply
senses.titleCN: 回信：书面答复
senses.definition: a letter or message sent in reply to one received
senses.definitionCN: 对收到的信件或消息所作的书面回复
senses.example: He sent an answer to the invitation the next day.
senses.exampleCN: 他第二天就回了邀请。
senses.why: The same exchange moves to paper: a letter asks, and a letter answers.
senses.whyCN: 同样的往来移到纸上：一封信提问，一封信回答。

senses.title: To open the door or pick up the phone
senses.titleCN: 应门；接听：回应呼叫
senses.definition: to go to the door or telephone when someone knocks or calls
senses.definitionCN: 有人敲门或来电时前去开门或接听
senses.example: No one answered when I knocked twice.
senses.exampleCN: 我敲了两次门，没人应。
senses.why: A knock and a ring are questions too; opening the door is the body's reply.
senses.whyCN: 敲门与铃声也是提问；开门就是身体作出的回答。

senses.title: To match or satisfy a need
senses.titleCN: 符合：满足需要或描述
senses.definition: to match a description or satisfy a need, often in the phrase answer to
senses.definitionCN: 与描述相符或满足需要，常用于短语 answer to
senses.example: The tool answers the need for a cheap repair.
senses.exampleCN: 这个工具满足了廉价修理的需要。
senses.why: A need is treated as a question, and the thing that fits it is its answer.
senses.whyCN: 需要被当作一个问题，而恰好合适的东西就是它的答案。

senses.title: To take responsibility for
senses.titleCN: 负责：为行为承担后果
senses.definition: to be responsible for something and accept blame or explain it, as in answer for
senses.definitionCN: 对某事负责并接受责怪或作出解释，如短语 answer for
senses.example: The manager must answer for the delay.
senses.exampleCN: 经理必须为这次延误负责。
senses.why: The old legal sense survives: a person called to account must give a formal reply to the charge.
senses.whyCN: 古老的法律义仍存：被要求交代的人必须对指控作出正式答复。

intro.en: Answer is an Old English word built from 'against' and 'swear', and its oldest sense is a formal reply to a charge.
intro.cn: answer 是一个由「对着」与「起誓」构成的古英语词，最古老的意义是对指控的正式回应。

items.en: Andswaru meant 'answer', literally a swearing against something, a reply made under challenge.
items.cn: andswaru 意为「回答」，字面是「对着某物起誓」，指在质问下作出的回应。

items.en: The prefix and- meant 'against, facing', the same element seen in modern words like withstand.
items.cn: 前缀 and- 意为「对着、面对」，同一成分也见于 withstand 等现代词。

items.en: Swerian meant 'to swear', so the original answer was a sworn statement made in reply.
items.cn: swerian 意为「起誓」，所以最初的 answer 是回应时作出的宣誓陈述。

items.en: The reconstructed Germanic form is andaswarō, with the same 'against-swear' structure.
items.cn: 重构的日耳曼语形式为 andaswarō，具有同样的「对着-起誓」结构。

items.en: Middle English answer kept both the legal reply and the everyday reply to a question.
items.cn: 中古英语 answer 同时保留法律回应与日常回答问题两种用法。

items.en: The word widened to doors, telephones and needs, but the shape of a reply to a call remained.
items.cn: 这个词扩展到门、电话与需要，但「对呼唤作出回应」的形态始终未变。

note.en: The look-alike group is the answer family; the near-meaning group holds replies, solutions and responses of different kinds.
note.cn: 形近组是 answer 词族；近义组收不同种类的回应、解答与答复。

entries.definition: Responsible to someone for something, or able to be answered.
entries.definitionCN: 对某事向某人负责的，或可被回答的。

entries.definition: A person who answers.
entries.definitionCN: 作出回答的人。

entries.definition: Not replied to.
entries.definitionCN: 未得到答复的。

entries.definition: A spoken or written response, often more formal than answer.
entries.definitionCN: 口头或书面的回应，常比 answer 更正式。

entries.definition: A reaction to something said or done.
entries.definitionCN: 对所说或所做之事的反应。

entries.definition: The way to solve a problem, rather than the words used to explain it.
entries.definitionCN: 解决问题的办法，而非解释它的言辞。

entries.definition: A quick, sharp reply, often to an insult.
entries.definitionCN: 迅速而尖刻的回应，常针对侮辱。

normalIntro.en: These hooks link the word to its 'swear against' origin, to the door, and to the difference between an answer and a solution.
normalIntro.cn: 下面几个钩子把这个词与「对着起誓」的来源、门口，以及「回答」与「解答」的差别连起来。

normal.en: The old word meant swear against: an answer is a reply made face to face.
normal.cn: 古词意为「对着起誓」：answer 就是面对面作出的回应。

normal.en: Say 'AHN-ser' in Britain and 'AN-ser' in America; the vowel shifts but the meaning does not.
normal.cn: 英式读「AHN-色」，美式读「AN-色」，元音变了，意思没变。

normal.en: You answer a question, answer the door, answer the phone: the same act of replying.
normal.cn: answer a question、answer the door、answer the phone：都是同一个回应动作。

normal.en: The answer to a question, not the answer of a question.
normal.cn: 是 the answer to a question，不是 the answer of a question。

normal.en: A solution fixes the problem; an answer replies to it. They are not always the same.
normal.cn: solution 解决问题，answer 回应问题；两者并不总是一回事。

abstract.en: An answer is a promise that the question had a shape after all.
abstract.cn: 回答是在承诺：那个问题终究是有形状的。

abstract.en: Some questions are answered by opening a door rather than by speaking.
abstract.cn: 有些问题不是靠说话回答的，而是靠把门打开。

abstract.en: The word assumes someone is waiting, which is why silence can feel like refusal.
abstract.cn: 这个词预设有人在等，所以沉默才会让人觉得是一种拒绝。

examples.en: Nobody could answer the final question.
examples.cn: 没人能回答最后那个问题。

examples.en: She answered the phone before the second ring.
examples.cn: 第二声铃响之前她就接了电话。

examples.en: His answer to the criticism was a long silence.
examples.cn: 他对批评的回应是一段长长的沉默。

dict_mnemonic.text: 谐音「安色」：安安静静地想一想，再给出一个合适的回答。

root: 古英语 and-（对着）+ swerian（起誓），andswaru 原指面对质问时作出的正式回应。

sensesIntro.en: The word starts as a formal reply, becomes the correct solution, extends to letters, doors and phones, then to matching a need and answering for a fault.
sensesIntro.cn: 这个词从正式回应出发，成为正确答案，扩展到信件、门与电话，再延伸到满足需要和为过错负责。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a question knocks like a fist on a door, and the reply opens it.
core.cn: 核心意象：问题像拳头一样敲门，回应把门打开。

branches.en: THE REPLY: the first two senses are the spoken response and its correct form.
branches.cn: 回应线：前两个义项是口头回答及其正确形式。

branches.en: THE LETTER: the third sense writes the reply down and sends it back.
branches.cn: 书信线：第三个义项把回应写下来送回去。

branches.en: THE DOOR: the fourth sense answers a knock or a ring with the body.
branches.cn: 门口线：第四个义项用身体回应敲门或铃声。

branches.en: THE FIT: the fifth sense treats a need as a question the object answers.
branches.cn: 契合线：第五个义项把需要当作问题，由物件来回答。

branches.en: THE ACCOUNT: the sixth sense is the legal reply a responsible person must give.
branches.cn: 交代线：第六个义项是负责人必须作出的法律回应。

intro.en: The verb and noun take -able, -er and un- to mark responsibility, the person and the missing reply.
intro.cn: 动词与名词接 -able、-er 与 un-，标示责任、人物与「未获回应」。

latinIntro.en: The word is Germanic; the suffixes are English, though -able came through French from Latin.
latinIntro.cn: 这个词属日耳曼语；后缀为英语所有，尽管 -able 是经法语来自拉丁语。

items.meaning: responsible, or able to be answered
items.meaningCN: 负有责任的，或可被回答的
items.example: Ministers are answerable to parliament.
items.exampleCN: 部长们对议会负责。

items.example: The answerer paused before speaking.
items.exampleCN: 回答者开口前停顿了一下。

items.example: The letter remained unanswered for weeks.
items.exampleCN: 那封信几周都没有回音。

items.example: Every question was answered in turn.
items.exampleCN: 每个问题都依次得到了回答。

items.example: The answering machine clicked on.
items.exampleCN: 应答机咔哒一声启动了。

items.example: The teacher kept the answer key in a drawer.
items.exampleCN: 老师把答案放在抽屉里。

items.meaning: a paper on which answers are written
items.example: Fill in the answer sheet with a pencil.
items.exampleCN: 用铅笔填写答题卡。

items.meaning: a device that records telephone messages
items.example: The answer machine picked up the call.
items.exampleCN: 答录机接起了电话。

definition_zh: 蚂蚁；蚁类；蚁群
definition_en: a small insect that lives in large groups in the ground, or the group of such insects as a kind
core_image: 一条细细的黑线在地板上移动，每一粒都是活的小东西
scene: 厨房地板上留下一粒糖，几只小虫排成一线。A single ant carried a crumb across the floor.
sceneCN: 这里 ant 是「蚂蚁」（第 1 个义项：单个蚂蚁）；句意为一只蚂蚁把面包屑搬过地板。画面里有地板、糖粒与排成线的蚂蚁。

pos.zh: 名词：蚂蚁；蚁类；蚁群

derivatives.zh: 由 ant 与 hill 复合，义为「蚁丘；蚁巢」
由 ant 与 eater 复合，义为「食蚁兽」
由 ant 与 like 复合，义为「像蚂蚁一样的」

senses.title: A single small insect
senses.titleCN: 蚂蚁：单个的小昆虫
senses.definition: a small insect with a thin waist that lives in an organized colony
senses.definitionCN: 腰部细窄、生活在有组织的蚁群中的小型昆虫
senses.example: An ant crawled up the side of the jar.
senses.exampleCN: 一只蚂蚁沿着罐子的侧面往上爬。
senses.why: Old English named the insect with a word probably meaning 'the biter' or 'the cutter', after its jaws.
senses.whyCN: 古英语给这种昆虫的名字，很可能意为「咬的东西」或「切的东西」，取自它的口器。

senses.title: The species or colony as a group
senses.titleCN: 蚁类；蚁群：作为整体的蚂蚁
senses.definition: the insects of this kind considered as a group, or a colony of them
senses.definitionCN: 把这类昆虫作为一个整体来看，或指一个蚁群
senses.example: The ant is one of the strongest creatures for its size.
senses.exampleCN: 就体型而言，蚂蚁是最强壮的生物之一。
senses.why: A single ant is almost meaningless alone; the word often stands for the colony that behaves like one body.
senses.whyCN: 单只蚂蚁几乎没有独立意义；这个词常代表像一具身体那样行动的整个蚁群。

intro.en: Ant is an Old English word whose modern form lost several sounds and gained an n from the article.
intro.cn: ant 是一个古英语词，现代形式丢掉了几个音，又从冠词那里得到了一个 n。

items.en: Ǣmete named the ant, and related forms appear across the Germanic languages.
items.cn: ǣmete 指蚂蚁，相关形式见于多种日耳曼语言。

items.en: The reconstructed form suggests an original meaning such as 'the biter' or 'the cutter', describing the insect's jaws.
items.cn: 重构形式暗示原义可能是「咬的东西」或「切的东西」，描述这种昆虫的口器。

items.en: Middle English used emmet and ampte; the shorter forms gradually displaced the longer ones.
items.cn: 中古英语用 emmet 与 ampte；较短的形式逐渐取代了较长的形式。

items.en: In phrases such as an emmet, the n of the article could be heard as part of the noun, a process called metanalysis.
items.cn: 在 an emmet 这类短语里，冠词的 n 可能被听成名词的一部分，这一过程称为「重新切分」。

items.en: The modern ant is short and plain, and it now appears in compounds such as anthill and anteater.
items.cn: 现代 ant 简短朴素，如今出现在 anthill 与 anteater 等复合词中。

note.en: The look-alike group gathers short words that resemble ant in sound; the near-meaning group gathers small social insects and their kin.
note.cn: 形近组收读音与 ant 相近的短词；近义组收小型社会性昆虫及其近亲。

entries.definition: The sister of one's father or mother.
entries.definitionCN: 父亲或母亲的姐妹。

entries.definition: One of the branched horns of a deer.
entries.definitionCN: 鹿的分叉角之一。

entries.definition: An animal that feeds mainly on ants.
entries.definitionCN: 主要以蚂蚁为食的动物。

entries.definition: The broad class of small six-legged creatures.
entries.definitionCN: 小型六足生物的统称。

entries.definition: A small pale insect that eats wood and lives in colonies.
entries.definitionCN: 吃木头、群居生活的小型浅色昆虫。

entries.definition: A flying insect that collects nectar and lives in hives.
entries.definitionCN: 采集花蜜、住在蜂巢里的飞行昆虫。

entries.definition: An insect with hard wing cases.
entries.definitionCN: 有坚硬鞘翅的昆虫。

normalIntro.en: These hooks use the lost n, the short sound, and the picture of a line of tiny carriers.
normalIntro.cn: 下面几个钩子用到丢掉的 n、短促的读音，以及「一列小小搬运工」的画面。

normal.en: Say 'ant': one short syllable, as small as the insect.
normal.cn: 读作「ant」，一个短音节，和那只昆虫一样小。

normal.en: It rhymes with pant and chant, which makes the short a easy to hold.
normal.cn: 它与 pant、chant 押韵，短 a 音很容易记住。

normal.en: The old word was emmet, and the n drifted over from 'an emmet'.
normal.cn: 古词是 emmet，n 是从「an emmet」那里漂过来的。

normal.en: An anthill is an ant hill, and an anteater eats ants; the compounds tell the story.
normal.cn: anthill 是蚂蚁的丘，anteater 是吃蚂蚁的兽；复合词自己会讲故事。

normal.en: One ant is tiny; a colony of ants can carry a whole leaf.
normal.cn: 一只蚂蚁很小，一群蚂蚁却能搬走整片叶子。

abstract.en: The ant is proof that a small body can do large work when it is not alone.
abstract.cn: 蚂蚁证明了：小身体只要不孤单，也能做大事。

abstract.en: We notice the single ant only when it is already a line.
abstract.cn: 我们注意到那只蚂蚁时，它往往已经排成了一条线。

abstract.en: The word is small, and most of what it means is the colony behind it.
abstract.cn: 这个词很小，而它含义的大部分是背后的蚁群。

examples.en: An ant can lift several times its own weight.
examples.cn: 一只蚂蚁能举起自身体重数倍的东西。

examples.en: The ants found the sugar within minutes.
examples.cn: 蚂蚁几分钟内就找到了糖。

examples.en: He watched a line of ants cross the path.
examples.cn: 他看着一列蚂蚁穿过小路。

dict_mnemonic.text: 谐音「安特」：安特趴在地上看蚂蚁，一看就是一下午。

root: 古英语 ǣmete（蚂蚁），源自日耳曼语，原义可能与「咬、切」有关；现代拼写受冠词重新切分影响。

sensesIntro.en: The word names one small insect and also the colony or kind as a whole.
sensesIntro.cn: 这个词既指一只小昆虫，也指作为整体的蚁群或蚁类。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a single tiny body moving in a line of identical bodies.
core.cn: 核心意象：一具微小的身体，在由相同身体排成的队列中移动。

branches.en: THE INDIVIDUAL: the first sense is one insect.
branches.cn: 个体线：第一个义项是一只昆虫。

branches.en: THE COLONY: the second sense is the group acting as one.
branches.cn: 群体线：第二个义项是作为一个整体行动的蚁群。

branches.en: THE LINE: one ant becomes visible only as part of a moving line.
branches.cn: 队列线：一只蚂蚁只有成为移动队列的一部分时才显眼。

branches.en: THE LOAD: a single ant carries a crumb, and the colony carries the whole store.
branches.cn: 负重线：单蚁搬一粒屑，蚁群搬整个粮仓。

branches.en: THE KIND: the word can stand for the species as a whole, as in the ant.
branches.cn: 种类线：这个词可代表整个蚁类，如 the ant。

intro.en: Ant forms compounds with hill, eater and like, and with roles inside the colony.
intro.cn: ant 与 hill、eater、like 以及蚁群内的角色构成复合词。

latinIntro.en: The word is Germanic; the compounds are English, though the second elements may come from Latin or French.
latinIntro.cn: 这个词属日耳曼语；复合词为英语所造，后半部分可能来自拉丁语或法语。

items.meaning: the mound over an ant colony
items.example: The children stepped over a low anthill.
items.exampleCN: 孩子们跨过一个低矮的蚁丘。

items.meaning: an animal that feeds on ants
items.example: The anteater has a long sticky tongue.
items.exampleCN: 食蚁兽有一条长长的黏舌。

items.example: The robot moved with an antlike gait.
items.exampleCN: 那个机器人以蚂蚁般的步态移动。

items.meaning: a small transparent colony kept for observation
items.meaningCN: 为观察而饲养的小型透明蚁群
items.example: He kept an ant farm on his desk.
items.exampleCN: 他在桌上养了一箱蚂蚁。

items.example: The ant colony moved into the wall.
items.exampleCN: 蚁群搬进了墙里。

items.meaning: an ant that gathers food and builds the nest
items.meaningCN: 采集食物、修筑巢穴的蚂蚁
items.example: A worker ant can carry twice its weight.
items.exampleCN: 一只工蚁能负重自身两倍。

items.meaning: the egg-laying female of a colony
items.meaningCN: 蚁群中负责产卵的雌蚁
items.example: The queen ant was hidden deep in the nest.
items.exampleCN: 蚁后藏在巢的深处。

items.meaning: a stinging ant known for painful bites
items.meaningCN: 以刺痛咬人著称的蚁种
items.example: A fire ant stung his hand.
items.exampleCN: 一只火蚁蜇了他的手。
